# DSH Keys Manager

[![npm downloads](https://img.shields.io/npm/dm/dsh-keys-manager)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Node](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%5E22.19%20%7C%7C%20%3E%3D24-339933)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-keys-manager)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%5E0.2.1--rc.2-0969DA)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns one provider API key into a managed pool.
It extends the Models page rather than replacing it: providers, models, and the
model picker stay where they are; only the API-key source moves behind the
manager.

## Features

- Several keys per provider, each with an alias and health state.
- One key pinned to a session, with round-robin selection for new sessions.
- Bounded retry on the same key, then automatic failover to another key.
- Exponential cooldown recovery, capped at seven days.
- A search-driven Keys Manager page on the plugin's own detail page.
- A "managed by Keys Manager" badge inside the existing Models provider cards.
- Extra built-in providers installed as ordinary `llm-pi-ai` routes.
- OAuth account sign-in for seven pi-ai-backed providers, stored beside
  the API keys.

### Extra providers

This catalog of 35 extra providers comes from
[oh-my-pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)'s provider catalog (MIT).

<details>
<summary>All 35 extra providers</summary>

| Provider | Route id | API key env |
|---|---|---|
| DeepInfra | `deepinfra` | `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY` |
| Novita | `novita` | `NOVITA_API_KEY` |
| StepFun | `stepfun` | `STEPFUN_API_KEY` |
| SambaNova | `sambanova` | `SAMBANOVA_API_KEY` |
| Qianfan | `qianfan` | `QIANFAN_API_KEY` |
| GMI Cloud | `gmi-cloud` | `GMI_API_KEY` |
| Synthetic | `synthetic` | `SYNTHETIC_API_KEY` |
| ZenMux | `zenmux` | `ZENMUX_API_KEY` |
| Kilo Gateway | `kilo` | `KILO_API_KEY` |
| NanoGPT | `nanogpt` | `NANO_GPT_API_KEY` |
| Venice AI | `venice` | `VENICE_API_KEY` |
| AIML API | `aimlapi` | `AIMLAPI_API_KEY` |
| AI& | `aiand` | `AIAND_API_KEY` |
| Helmcode | `helmcode` | `HELMCODE_API_KEY` |
| Alibaba Coding Plan | `alibaba-coding-plan` | `ALIBABA_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| MiniMax Coding (Global) | `minimax-code` | `MINIMAX_CODE_API_KEY` |
| MiniMax Coding (CN) | `minimax-code-cn` | `MINIMAX_CODE_CN_API_KEY` |
| Umans AI Coding Plan | `umans` | `UMANS_AI_CODING_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| Sakana AI | `sakana` | `SAKANA_API_KEY` |
| CoralBricks | `coralbricks` | `CORAL_API_KEY` |
| Wafer Serverless | `wafer-serverless` | `WAFER_SERVERLESS_API_KEY` |
| Alibaba Token Plan | `alibaba-token-plan` | `ALIBABA_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| Alibaba Token Plan (CN) | `alibaba-token-plan-cn` | `BAILIAN_TOKEN_PLAN_API_KEY` |
| Charm Hyper | `charm-hyper` | `CHARM_HYPER_API_KEY`, `HYPER_API_KEY` |
| LiteLLM Proxy | `litellm` | `LITELLM_API_KEY` |
| SiliconFlow | `siliconflow` | `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` |
| SiliconFlow (CN) | `siliconflow-cn` | `SILICONFLOW_CN_API_KEY` |
| Zhipu Coding Plan | `zhipu-coding-plan` | `ZHIPU_API_KEY` |
| Abliteration | `abliteration` | `ABLITERATION_API_KEY`, `ABLIT_KEY` |
| ClinePass | `cline-pass` | `CLINE_API_KEY` |
| Command Code | `commandcode` | `COMMAND_CODE_API_KEY`, `COMMANDCODE_API_KEY` |
| CoreWeave Serverless Inference | `coreweave` | `COREWEAVE_API_KEY` |
| Fire Pass | `firepass` | `FIREPASS_API_KEY` |
| Ollama Cloud | `ollama-cloud` | `OLLAMA_CLOUD_API_KEY` |
| Yolo Auto | `yolo-auto` | `YOLO_AUTO_API_KEY` |

Where two variables are listed, either is accepted; the first is the primary.

CoreWeave Serverless Inference also needs `COREWEAVE_PROJECT=<team>/<project>` in the DSH process environment before it is added.

</details>

## Quick start

### Install — DeepSeek Harness Desktop / Web

In the DeepSeek Harness Desktop or Web app, open **Plugins**, click
**Add plugin**, enter `dsh-keys-manager` in the package field, and click
**Install**. When the install finishes, choose **Enable now** so the plugin is
switched on.

Through the wizard, the app installs the same published npm package as the
CLI path below, already carrying its built bundle. Refresh the DeepSeek
Harness page afterwards so the browser half is fetched.

### Install — published package

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-keys-manager
```

### Install — local checkout

```sh
git clone https://github.com/btspoony/dsh-keys-manager
cd dsh-keys-manager
pnpm i
dsh plugin --profile web link .
```

The two CLI paths differ in where the build output comes from: `dsh plugin
--profile web add dsh-keys-manager` installs the published npm tarball, which
ships the built `lib/` and the client bundle. The local
`dsh plugin --profile web link .` path runs `prepare` during `pnpm i`, which
builds `lib/` and the client bundle, so the clone flow above includes that
build step; `prepack` builds the same output when the package is packed or
published.

Refresh the Web page after installing so the browser half is fetched.

## Usage

Open **Plugins → Keys Manager → View** (rendered as
`Plugins → 密钥管理 → 查看` in the Chinese locale). The manager renders on the
plugin's detail page, between its description and its included rows, matching
the shipped plugin configuration cards.

1. Search for a provider. Existing DSH providers appear first; the plugin also
   ships the curated extra catalog described above.
2. Adopt a provider. For an existing provider the manager imports the
   currently resolved credential, writes a broker reference into the provider
   profile, and leaves the original key in the credential store so release can
   restore it.
3. Add more keys with an alias. Every key is stored in the Harness credential
   store under its own reference; the manager state document never contains a
   key literal.
4. Manage a key from the three-dot menu: rename, pause/resume, delete. A key
   row shows status, last use, and the recovery time while cooling.
5. Tune retry count (1–3), base cooldown, and recovery grace in the settings
   card.

### OAuth accounts

Providers that ship a native OAuth sign-in offer two ways to join the pool:
**Add key** stores a static API key, while **Add account** runs the
provider's OAuth sign-in flow and stores the resulting grant as an account
row in the same pool.

Supported providers — the seven whose OAuth flows `llm-pi-ai` implements:
Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Coding, OpenAI Codex, OpenRouter, Radius,
and xAI.

The increment-1 model is honest about scope: **API keys form the selection
ring** — sticky sessions, round-robin, retry failover, and cooldowns
operate across the provider's API keys — while **one projected OAuth grant
serves its provider**: the account whose grant is projected answers
requests directly, and one active grant per provider is kept. Per-account
ranking (rotating or load-balancing between accounts) is future work. An
account row's counters reflect that account's own successes and failures,
not a per-account traffic split. When the projected grant fails (expired
or refresh rejected), the account cools down. On a key-capable route the
pool falls back to the provider's key pool; an OAuth-only route has no
API-key pool and stops serving requests until an account is signed in
again. Recovery is a manual re-login from the account menu.

Adding an account stores only the provider-issued grant in the Harness
credential store, behind the account's `grantRef`; the manager state keeps
the reference plus non-sensitive metadata (email, account id, expiry) — the
same secret-free layout as API keys.

### Selection and failure policy

- **Sticky session**: the first request of a session selects a key and binds
  it for that session/provider pair. Later requests reuse it.
- **Round robin**: a new session advances the provider cursor and takes the
  next healthy key.
- **Retry**: a failing request is retried on the same key `retryCount` times.
- **Switch**: after the retry budget is spent, the failing key is marked
  cooling, and the session is rebound to another healthy key.
- **Cooldown**: the first failure cools a key for `baseCooldownMs`. A failure
  while cooling, or within `recoveryGraceMs` after recovery, doubles the
  next cooldown. A long healthy gap resets the escalation. The hard cap is
  seven days.
- **Recovery**: the key is automatically selectable again when its cooldown
  expires; no manual reset is required.
- **Delegation**: request-shaped failures such as
  `CONTEXT_WINDOW_EXCEEDED` and cancellation never cool a key. When no
  alternate key exists, the manager delegates to the composition's normal
  retry/fallback policy.

## Configuration & data

Manager metadata lives at:

```text
$DSH_HOME/keys-manager/state.json
```

with owner-only permissions. It contains aliases, credential references,
health counters, session bindings, and provider adoption facts. API key
literals live only in the Harness credential store. The file is written
atomically through a temporary file and a rename.

Each managed provider profile points its `apiKeyEnv` at a broker reference
such as `KEYSMGR_ZAI_CODING_CN_3FA2C1`. The Host credential layer answers that
reference per request with the session's selected key. The Models page sees
the profile as configured; writing directly to the broker reference is
refused with a pointer to the manager.

### OAuth2 extension point

The state shape already distinguishes `kind: "api-key"` from `kind: "oauth"`
and keeps a nullable `oauth` object beside the credential reference. A future
account flow can add records under `keys-manager/<provider>/<key>` without
rewriting existing rows. Providers whose only authentication is OAuth are
reported as unsupported in this version rather than being treated as API-key
providers.

## Provider classification

Every provider card carries its origin:

- **DSH built-in** (`DSH 内置`) — a route from the shipped DSH pi-ai catalog.
- **Plugin built-in** (`插件内置`) — a route from this plugin's extra catalog
  in `src/providers.ts`.
- **Custom** (`自定义`) — a hand-declared route in the active profile.

The following DSH built-ins are explicitly outside single-key pool management:

| Provider | Why |
|---|---|
| `amazon-bedrock` | AWS credential chain (profile, IAM keys, ECS/IRSA/EC2), not one API key |
| `cloudflare-ai-gateway` | API key plus a Cloudflare account ID and gateway ID |
| `cloudflare-workers-ai` | API key plus a Cloudflare account ID |
| `openai-codex` | ChatGPT OAuth sign-in only; no API-key credential — usable as an [OAuth account](#oauth-accounts) instead of a key |

All other DSH catalog routes expose an API-key credential. Providers that
also support OAuth (Anthropic, GitHub Copilot, Kimi Coding, OpenAI Codex,
OpenRouter, Radius, xAI) remain manageable through their API-key path, and
their OAuth sign-in is available as [OAuth accounts](#oauth-accounts).

## Documentation

| Doc | Content |
|---|---|
| [Development](docs/development.md) | build and dev workflow, repository layout |
| [Release](docs/release.md) | CI checks and the npm release flow |
| [Known limits](docs/known-limits.md) | current design boundaries, including deferred providers |

Chinese versions: [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md) and the `*.zh-CN.md`
files in `docs/` — [开发](docs/development.zh-CN.md) ·
[发布](docs/release.zh-CN.md) · [已知限制](docs/known-limits.zh-CN.md).
Current design boundaries at a glance:
[Known limits](docs/known-limits.md).

## License

Released under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

dsh-reference-anything

One `@` for them all. **English** · [简体中文](./README_zh-CN.md) [📰 News](#-news) · [🧭 Roadmap](#-roadmap) · [📦 Installation](#-installation) · [🚀 Usage](#-usage) · [🐛 Report Bug][github-issues-link] [![][stable-version-shield]][stable-version-link] [![][alpha-version-shield]][alpha-version-link] [![][typescript-shield]][typescript-link] [![][dsh-plugin-shield]][repository-link]
[![][github-stars-shield]][github-stars-link] [![][github-forks-shield]][github-forks-link] [![][github-issues-shield]][github-issues-link] [![][github-license-shield]][github-license-link]
![awesome · DSH plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com/badge.svg) [![][npm-downloads-shield]][npm-package-link] [![dshfind](https://dshfind.com/api/badge/Chael-Chael/dsh-reference-anything?lang=zh)](https://dshfind.com/zh/plugins/Chael-Chael/dsh-reference-anything?ref=badge)
**Reference Anything is an enhancement for the DeepSeek Harness (DSH) `@` menu.** It brings files, sessions, local agents, web chats, cloud drives, and local plugins into one searchable menu, so you can mention the context you need without switching tools or copying content manually. After typing `@`, you can browse and click items in the menu with your mouse, or use the keyboard to enter text, search, and narrow down the results. When a folder is selected, press `Tab` to enter it and continue browsing, or `Enter` to insert the folder reference. Use one `@` menu to reference: - 🧩 DSH commands and Skills - 📁 Workspace files and folders - 💬 DSH session history - 🖥️ **Local Agent conversations:** bundled scanning and read-only parsers for 29 source formats, including Claude Code, Codex and Cursor; optional import into DSH through Chat Import. Live acceptance coverage is recorded separately. - ✨ **Added by this plugin — highlight: Historical conversations from web chatbots including ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and Kimi** - ☁️ **Added by this plugin: Files from cloud drives connected through OpenList** - 🧩 **Added by this plugin: Installed and configured local DSH plugins, without repeatedly hunting through directories** Beyond extending what `@` can reference, Reference Anything also enhances the `@` menu itself: - Customize visible groups: enable or hide `Commands`, `Skills`, files, DSH sessions, local agent conversations, external conversations, cloud-drive files, and local plugins, then arrange them in any order - Customize shortcuts: assign your own shortcuts to source groups, web providers, local agents, and cloud-drive mounts - Customize result counts: set each group's collapsed row count and hard candidate cap independently - Choose how to browse: expand or collapse individual groups, or use DSH's native scrolling list - Enhanced visual icons and commands: distinguish reference sources with type icons and platform logos
Native DSH display Reference Anything icon enhancements
Type `@`, search across enabled sources, and insert the selected reference into the current task. Each source keeps its own access and loading behavior: files use DSH's permission-constrained tools, DSH sessions use the native session-reference protocol, local agent transcripts are streamed straight off disk, cloud-drive files are fetched a window at a time over the drive's own API, and external conversation bodies are read on demand. **The External conversations group** — and only that group — uses OpenCLI to reach AI chat sessions you are already logged into. By default it stores conversation titles locally and the agent fetches remote content on demand; an optional offline-mirror mode stores the latest complete bodies locally instead. **Local agent conversations need none of that**: those transcripts are already files on your own disk, so that group reads them directly, with no browser, no OpenCLI, and nothing mirrored. > [!NOTE] > DSH is currently in Beta, so its underlying capabilities and interfaces may change as it evolves. This plugin will adapt alongside those changes. Because of some current DSH limitations, parts of the implementation may not yet be ideal; we will continue to follow DSH updates and improve the plugin over time. See the relevant sections below for specific limitations and usage notes. ## 📰 News ### 0.5.0 Preview · Feature Demos This update also adds unified local pagination, resumable long-text reads and message/tool search, rechecks source switches on every read, and moves non-local tools to external_reference_list/read. See the [release and migration guide](./docs/release-v0.5.0.md). Version 0.5.0 is not yet published. #### Import Past Conversations into DSH and Pick Up Where You Left Off Want to continue an existing local session without copying and pasting chat logs or treating old threads purely as static context? Now, when you find a local session in the `@` menu, you have two ways to use it: - **Reference as context (`Enter`)**: Insert the session directly as a reference; - **Import and continue chatting (`Tab`)**: Open the action menu, select **Import**, and confirm to bring the entire conversation history into DSH and keep chatting seamlessly! (Prefer a faster workflow? You can disable the confirmation prompt in Settings.) > 💡 **Note**: Importing requires `dsh-chat-import` v0.26.1 or a compatible newer version to be installed and enabled. ![Press Enter to reference a session, or Tab to open the action menu and import history; uses mock data.](./release-notes/0.5.0/demos/agent-import.gif) #### One-Click Upgrade for `dsh-chat-import` Right from the Menu If an outdated version of `dsh-chat-import` prevents you from using chat import or handoff summaries, you no longer need to update it manually. Simply click the **upgrade prompt** right inside the menu to update to v0.26.1 or later. If prompted after the upgrade, restart DSH to apply the changes. ![Upgrade dsh-chat-import from the menu and view the simulated restart prompt in settings.](./release-notes/0.5.0/demos/chat-import-upgrade.gif) #### Type `@plugin:` to Reference Installed Plugins Directly Want your Agent to troubleshoot a plugin issue or inspect its source code? Digging through deep system folders just to find the installation path is a hassle. Now you can simply type `@plugin:`, search for the plugin name, and press `Enter` to pass its installation directory straight to the Agent (supports all plugins currently installed in your DSH environment). ![Filter local plugins in the @plugin: menu and press Enter to insert the plugin directory reference.](./release-notes/0.5.0/demos/local-plugins.gif) #### Custom Shortcuts to Narrow Down Your Search Scope Instantly Tired of scrolling through a cluttered `@` menu full of files, folders, and different sources just to find a past conversation? You can now assign **custom shortcuts** to different chat sources in Settings (multiple shortcuts can be separated by commas), allowing you to filter by category and narrow down your search scope right as you type: - **Search across a combined group**: Not sure where a conversation happened? Assign the same shortcut (e.g., `chat`) to both Local Agents and Web Chats, then type `@chat:` to narrow your search exclusively to those sources; - **Target a specific source**: When you know exactly where to look, use a dedicated shortcut like `@codex:` to filter exclusively for Codex sessions. ![Configure shared shortcuts in settings, then search sessions using both shared and source-specific shortcuts.](./release-notes/0.5.0/demos/shortcuts.gif) #### Browse Folders Directly in the `@` Menu — No Need to Type Full Paths Want to reference a deeply nested folder without memorizing or typing out its full path? You can now navigate folder hierarchies directly inside the `@` file menu: - **Open subfolder**: Select a folder and press `Tab` to step inside; - **Go back**: Use the breadcrumb navigation bar at the top of the menu; - **Insert reference**: Press `Enter` on your target folder to insert it directly into your chat. ![Press Tab in the file menu to enter subdirectories, navigate back, and press Enter to reference a folder.](./release-notes/0.5.0/demos/folders.gif) - **2026-10-12 · v0.4.4** — Added local plugin discovery to the `@` menu, configurable source and provider shortcuts, improved picker icons and folder insertion, and added the `model` command entry. - **2026-10-06 · v0.4.3** — Reference Anything now supports DSH Desktop! Enjoy a refreshed and optimized settings page! - **2026-09-28 · v0.4.2 — Important update** — Fixed a fatal plugin compatibility error with the current DSH interface. Restart DSH if asked, then open **Settings → Reference Anything**. Desktop uses a separate plugin profile; plugins installed in the Web profile are not automatically enabled in Desktop. See the [official desktop documentation](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/master/apps/desktop/README.md). ### DSH Market Open [Reference Anything on DSH Market](https://dshmarket.com/p/Chael-Chael/dsh-reference-anything/), or search for `dsh-reference-anything` in the in-app market. If the market is not installed, use **Add plugin** with `dshmarket` in Desktop; for Web, run: ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web add dshmarket ``` ### Web CLI ```powershell dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-reference-anything ``` The installed version depends on the selected channel; this README describes v0.5.0. ### Optional: Connect web AI chats Only web chats need this step. It uses OpenCLI 2.0.0 installed as a runtime dependency and updated together with this plugin; installs the bundled adapters for all six platforms; starts or refreshes Browser Bridge; and opens the OpenCLI Browser Bridge page in the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/opencli/ildkmabpimmkaediidaifkhjpohdnifk). Confirm the extension installation, then return and click **Recheck setup**. Any remaining failed check displays its own recovery action. For a custom global OpenCLI, install it manually and enter its full executable path in settings. The default opencli always uses the plugin dependency: ```powershell npm install --global "@jackwener/opencli@2.0.0" opencli plugin install file:///C:/path/to/dsh-reference-anything/opencli-plugin opencli daemon restart ``` Replace `C:/path/to/dsh-reference-anything` with the repository location. When multiple browser profiles are connected, select and apply one directly in the failed check. OpenCLI updates with this plugin; the browser store updates the extension separately. ## 🚀 Usage Reference Anything registers eight sources in the native DSH `@` menu rather than introducing a separate search interface. Settings let you choose which groups appear, their order, their collapsed row count, their hard candidate cap, and whether groups use plugin-owned collapse actions or the native scrolling list. A separate one-click control switches the visible picker back to DSH's official file/session list without stopping the plugin, synchronization service, local data, or model-facing tools; the same control restores the Reference Anything picker at any time. 1. Type `@` to browse sources, or enter a keyword such as `@cache-design`. 2. Click a result, or select it with the arrow keys and press `Enter`. For workspace folders, `Tab` opens the folder and `Enter` inserts a reference. 3. Add your request and send it: “Use this Codex conversation and project folder to check whether the earlier plan has been implemented.” For web chats, complete the connection steps above, then choose platforms, browser profile, storage mode, and history range under **Settings → Reference Anything → Web AI conversation sync settings** and start syncing. For cloud files, connect OpenList and add a mount in Settings. The default **Read bodies on demand** mode stores only the title index locally and uses the browser when an agent needs the conversation. Choose **Store full bodies locally** for offline reading and full-text search. The plugin checks for new versions when it loads; release notes are available in Settings, and installed updates take effect after restarting DSH. > [!NOTE] > OpenCLI may open or reuse browser windows while syncing web chats or reading bodies. Keep them available until the operation finishes. Sync speed depends on the platform, history size, and browser connection. ### Shortcut examples These examples use the current defaults. After changing shortcuts, use the values shown in Settings. | Input | What it finds | | --- | --- | | `@file:README` | Workspace files and folders | | `@session:` | DSH session history | | `@agent:` / `@codex:` | Local agent history / Codex only | | `@chat:` / `@chatgpt:cache` | Web chats / matching ChatGPT chats | | `@drive:` | Connected cloud drives | | `@plugin:` | Local DSH plugins | | `@command:` / `@skill:` | Commands / Skills | Under **General**, set shortcuts for groups, web providers, local agents, and cloud mounts. Separate multiple shortcuts with commas: set the file group to `file,f`, then use `@f:README`. A shortcut can target multiple sources. Full-width colons (`：`) are also supported. ### 🧩 One `@` menu, multiple sources The `@` menu contains eight groups: `Commands`, `Skills`, `Files and folders`, `DSH sessions`, `Local agent conversations`, `External conversations`, `Cloud drive files`, and `All local plugins`. The cloud-drive group browses folders and supported files from drives connected through OpenList; access is read-only, and connections are managed in Settings. Each group shows six rows before its expand action by default and accepts a separate hard candidate cap from 1 to 50. In collapse mode, each expand action reveals five more rows and updates the mounted menu without jumping back to the top; collapse restores the configured compact count. The external-conversation group keeps its sync action first and updates that row and the visible results in place while synchronization runs and completes. Under `Settings → Reference Anything → General`, you can enable or disable groups, reorder them, assign an optional custom shortcut (for example `f` for Files, then use `@f:notes`), and choose **Collapse / expand** or **Native DSH scrolling**. #### ⌨️ @Commands — DSH native commands To browse commands, use `@command:`; selecting one hands `/command` back to DSH's native slash pipeline.

#### 🛠️ @Skills — DSH skill library To browse skills, use `@skill:`; selecting one inserts `/skill` for DSH's native skill handling.

#### 📁 @Files and folders — workspace files and directories Type `@file:` in the input box to browse files and folders through DSH's official file-reference Remote.

**Features:** - Uses the official `@path` / `@"path with spaces"` grammar and canonical file candidate service - Files and folders become native references; press `Tab` on a folder to browse inside it, or `Enter` to insert it #### 💬 @DSH sessions — DSH session history Type `@session:` to browse DSH sessions through the official session-reference Remote.

Selected sessions use DSH's canonical `dsh-session:` mention and native session appearance. Snapshot preparation and resolution remain owned by DSH rather than this plugin. #### 🖥️ @Local agent conversations — transcripts from local agent CLIs Type `@agent:` to search and reference conversations saved by other local agent tools. Source switches, additional directories and workspace scope still apply; settings show source paths, counts and scan errors. Enter inserts a reference, including recoverable images through DSH attachments; viewing images requires a vision-capable model. Confirmed empty conversations are hidden; read errors remain visible. Local references now store a readable source, path and session ID; reselect references created with the old local URI protocol. When you send local references, the plugin appends one aggregated background after each user message. The model reads `ref: {source, path, sessionId}` with a content `revision`. `reference_list` discovers local sessions; `reference_read` reads `messages`, `tools` or `images`; `reference_search` searches message/tool text; `reference_image` returns actual pixels. Use `from` for both scope and starting position: `messages` uses `messageId`; `tools` uses `toolId` with an optional owning `messageId`; `images` uses `imageId` with an optional owning `messageId`. Copy the complete `next` object into `from` to continue. Long text uses a Unicode code-point `textOffset`, preserving every remaining character rather than keeping only the head and tail. Source-provided summaries use `role: "summary"`; source limitations use an English `notice`. Source content is never translated. `reference-mention.maxTextBytes` caps all new reference contexts in one pre-step batch at 16 KiB by default; estimated remaining context can reduce it. `reference-tool.maxTextBytes` separately caps each local tool text result at 16 KiB. Unknown capacity leaves only bounded metadata and a notice; metadata that cannot fit fails explicitly. Previews contain a continuous recent suffix, with a continuation for an oversized final message. Images have a separate 10 MiB limit. Every new read checks the enabled source, allowed real path and session identity; no per-session grant is needed for local references. After a version change, restart `reference_read` with the same `ref`, `part: "messages"`, and omit both `revision` and `from`. No full-text snapshots or cross-call parsed-body caches are saved. Other sources retain their existing URI-based protocol under `external_reference_list` and `external_reference_read`. Import status, session import and handoff summaries use the optional Chat Import API. Install or upgrade the independent plugin from settings when needed; Reference Anything does not install it on startup. An unavailable API leaves import status unknown and does not stop local scanning or reference reading. Tab retains the configured import and summary actions and confirmation flow. **Supported sources:** Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Antigravity, Reasonix, opencode, mimocode, zcode, Grok Build, OpenClaw, Pi, Hermes, Kimi, Kilo Code, Qoder, ChatGPT exports, WorkBuddy, Qwen Code, Continue, Cline, Goose, DSH 4, Zed, Crush, Teleagent, Trae Work, Vibe, and DSH. **Features:** - Automatically detects conversation history and shows the number found for each agent - Lets you enable agents independently or choose a custom history folder - Searches all detected conversations by default, with an option to limit results to the current workspace - Automatically previews recent body text; reads numbered messages, associated tool details and images on demand - Supports agent-specific prefixes such as `@codex:`, `@claude-code:`, and `@gemini-cli:` References read local history without modifying it. Claude Code and Codex adapters have been checked against real transcripts; other formats are primarily fixture-tested and may vary by tool version. Database reads for opencode, mimocode, and zcode require `node:sqlite` in the DSH host runtime. #### 🧩 @Local plugins — installed and configured plugins Use `@plugin:` to find plugins. Settings can also show only running plugins or hide official DeepSeek plugins. Under **Settings → Reference Anything → General**, the **All local plugins** switch enables or disables this group immediately; the choice is saved. It is enabled by default, with six collapsed rows and a candidate cap of 50. The list uses the active DSH loader's composed entries and lifecycle state, supplemented by declared profile bundles and installed packages with DSH bundle/client metadata. Ordinary dependencies are excluded. Running, disabled, and not-running states describe host entries; packages without a host entry are shown as not running. Selecting a plugin inserts its name and, when available, a native reference to its real local directory. File access still uses DSH's existing tools and permissions. #### 🌐 @External conversations — external conversation platforms Supports historical conversations from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, Grok, and Kimi.

**Store full bodies locally** enables offline reading of synchronized text; it does not mean attachments are saved offline. Automatic and startup sync are off by default and can be enabled in Settings. **Platform filtering:** - Use `@chatgpt:cache` or `@claude:refactor` to filter a specific platform - Short aliases are also accepted, such as `@gpt:` and `@ds:` - Entering `@claude` alone lists recent conversations for that platform **Search capabilities:** - **Title match:** fuzzy search on conversation titles - **Content search:** available only in **Store full bodies locally** mode; if title matches are insufficient, synchronized bodies are searched and matching excerpts are shown in the candidate list - **Provider and account isolation:** history is maintained separately by Provider and account scope - `@` search uses the account scope cached by the latest sync and never probes the browser; after a sync observes an account switch, it exposes only that account while older rows remain available in conversation management for cleanup **Reference display:** after selection, the draft shows a native removable DSH reference with the Provider logo. Its stable serialized form is: ```text @[ChatGPT·Conversation title](dsh-ref:) ``` Opening the source URL happens only in the UI; the URL is never injected into model context. A Web conversation reference initially contains only a safe pointer; if the model needs the body, it calls `external_reference_read` on demand. #### ☁️ @Cloud drive files — files connected through OpenList Type `@drive:` to browse folders and reference files from cloud drives connected through OpenList. Common providers include OneDrive, Aliyun Drive, Baidu Netdisk, Quark, 115, 123, Dropbox, Google Drive/Photos, and Yandex. The host source stays registered, so an already-inserted reference still expands and `external_reference_read` still works; only the menu entry is gone until you switch back. ## 🔄 How External Conversation References Work ```text DSH Web / Desktop @chat: ↕ Host Remote DSH Host + reference_anything index / optional body mirror ↕ execFile(opencli, argv) opencli-plugin-dsh-chat-history ↕ OpenCLI daemon + official Browser Bridge ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini / DeepSeek / Grok / Kimi ``` ### 🤖 Model-facing Protocol A reference produces an untrusted-data envelope alongside the current user request. # dsh-video-preview

为 [DeepSeek Harness（DSH）](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的右侧「文档预览」面板
增加视频播放能力的**本地增量插件**：打开 `.mp4 / .m4v / .webm / .mov / .ogv` 时显示播放器，
支持播放、暂停、拖动进度；不修改 DSH 自带文件，可随时整体卸载。

English: a **local, additive DSH plugin** that teaches the Sidebar document preview to play video files
(streaming over HTTP, in-memory playback on the Desktop shell so seeking works). No shipped DSH file is
modified; removing the bundle restores the original behavior. See [English quick start](#english-quick-start).

---

## 1. 功能

- 在右侧文档预览 / 浮层面板中直接播放视频，替换原来的「该格式文件暂时无法预览」空状态。
- 拖动进度、音量、倍速等使用浏览器原生 `<video>` 控件。
- 已经打开着的「不可预览」视频标签会在插件加载后自动切换为播放器，无需刷新页面。
- 其他预览器（文本 / Markdown / 代码 / 图片 / PDF / HTML / Office / Excel）行为完全不变。
- 可随时删除：`plugin_manager remove_bundle @local/dsh-video-preview`。

## 2. 背景与根因

- **缺少渲染器**：DSH 的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-documentpreview` 只注册了
  文本 / Markdown / 代码 / 图片 / PDF / HTML / Office / Excel 渲染器；`mp4`、`webm`、`mov` 等
  被列入 `UNVIEWABLE_BINARY_EXTENSIONS`，没有匹配渲染器时固定显示「该格式文件暂时无法预览」。
  插件通过公开的 `ctx.documentPreviews.register(...)` + keyed 槽 `sidebar.right.tab.document`
  注册一个视频渲染器，即可复用整套文档预览外壳（标签、路径栏、刷新、自动刷新）。
- **Desktop 拖动进度不可用**：Desktop 页面来自自定义协议 `dsh-app://app/`，响应由 Electron
  主进程合成后返回；Electron 已知缺陷使这类媒体响应不可 seek（`video.seekable.end() === 0`），
  即使返回正确的 `206` / `Content-Range`。上游 issue：
  [electron#38749](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/38749)、
  [electron#51442](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/51442)。
  本项目不改 Electron 主进程，而是在渲染器里按页面来源选择播放方式。

## 3. 方案与实现

```
浏览器                                Host（同一 DSH 进程）
┌─────────────────────────┐          ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
│ @local/dsh-video-preview│          │ @local/dsh-video-preview (index.js)│
│ client.js               │          │ GET/HEAD /api/video-preview        │
│ · documentPreviews      │ <video>  │ · 校验 session + 路径 + 扩展名     │
│   .register(video)      │ ───────► │ · workspaceFiles.stat 取 size/version│
│ · keyed body 注册        │  Range   │ · 512 KiB 分块回传 200/206         │
│ · 中英文字典             │ ◄─────── │ · 416/404/415/499 语义完整         │
└─────────────────────────┘          │ 复用 connection 认证栅栏            │
                                     └────────────────────────────────────┘
```

渲染器声明 `loading: 'renderer'`，由组件自己决定播放源：

| 页面来源 | 播放源 | 行为 |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP(S) 网页端 | `<video src="/api/video-preview?...">` | 原生 `Range` 流式读取，512 KiB/块，可 seek，内存平坦 |
| Desktop `dsh-app://app/` | Session Remote 整文件读取 → Blob URL | ≤ 32 MiB 全量读入，可任意拖动；> 32 MiB 仍流式播放并提示不可拖动 |

- 路由复用 `ctx.connection.fetch.register`（与自带 `/api/file` 相同的认证栅栏），
  `ctx.workspaceFiles` 取元数据、`ctx.sessions` + `ctx.sandboxPolicy` 解析会话工作区；
  只允许上述视频扩展名，不是通用文件服务器。
- 流式播放失败时只回退一次整文件读取；回退失败或超限时显示本地化提示，
  工具栏的「打开 / 显示文件位置」按钮始终可用。
- 全部资源用 `ctx.effect(...)` 注册，卸载即回收；不新增定时器、轮询或 DOM 监听。
- Blob URL 在换标签、刷新、卸载时 `URL.revokeObjectURL`，不长期占用内存。

## 4. 目录

| 路径 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| `plugin/` | **DSH bundle 包目录**（安装 target） |
| `plugin/package.json` | bundle 清单：`dsh.bundle.patch` + `dsh.client`（`platform: web`, `immediately`） |
| `plugin/cordis.patch.yml` | 只 `insert` 一行 host 插件 `video-preview`，无配置、无覆盖 |
| `plugin/index.js` | Host 半：认证、Range 解析、分块流式读取 |
| `plugin/client.js` | 浏览器半：渲染器注册、keyed body、中英文案、双播放路径 |
| `plugin/locale/{en,zh}.json` | 插件列表显示的名称与描述 |
| `plugin/icon.svg` | 原创图标 |
| `tests/test-client.mjs` | 离线装配测试：模拟模块加载器，校验 `inject` / 渲染器元数据 / 槽注册 |
| `tests/test-host.mjs` | 离线集成测试：真实临时文件跑 HEAD/200/206/416/404/415 与分块读取 |
| `tools/asar_*.py` | 只读解析 Electron `app.asar` 的小工具，用于复核 DSH 内部契约 |
| `samples/video-preview-test.mp4` | 4 秒 640×360 H.264+AAC 自测素材（含音轨） |

## 5. 安装

前提：DSH 是 Web 或 Desktop 组合（必须存在 `ui-sidebar-documentpreview`；headless / SDK / ACP
等无浏览器 UI 的组合装了也不会显示），版本兼容性见第 8 节。

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chenyitao123/dsh-video-preview.git
```

然后任选一种：

1. **让 DSH Agent 安装**：`plugin_manager install_bundle`，`target` 指向克隆目录下的
   `dsh-video-preview/plugin` 绝对路径。
2. **设置界面**：设置 → 插件 → 从本地目录安装，选择同一个 `plugin/` 目录。
3. 也可以用压缩包：把 `plugin/` 打成 zip（或使用仓库 Release 附件），解压后同样指向 `plugin/`。

安装结果应为 `application: applied`，设置 → 插件出现「视频预览 / Video Preview」。
安装只写**当前 profile**（`package.json` 的 bundle 列表 + `node_modules` 里的链接），
不改 DSH 全局安装目录，也不影响同机其他 profile。

> 注意：如果安装时选择本地目录链接（junction），不要移动或删除 `plugin/`；
> 需要迁移时先 `remove_bundle`，拷贝到新位置后重新安装。

## 6. 验证

```bash
node tests/test-client.mjs
node tests/test-host.mjs
```

两者应输出 `all assertions passed`。

运行中验证：

1. 设置 → 插件，能看到「视频预览 / Video Preview」条目和图标。
2. 打开任意视频文件：应出现播放器；播放、暂停、拖动进度正常。
3. 用 `samples/video-preview-test.mp4` 验证音量（该文件带 AAC 音轨；无音轨视频的音量控件
   会被 Chromium 禁用，这是浏览器行为）。
4. 关闭标签后 Host 的流请求中止；换标签/刷新后 Blob URL 被回收。

## 7. 卸载

```text
plugin_manager  action: remove_bundle  target: @local/dsh-video-preview
```

手动删除等价步骤：

1. 从当前 profile 的 `package.json` 删除 `dsh.profile.bundles` 里的 `@local/dsh-video-preview`
   以及 `dependencies` 里的同名项。
2. 删除该 profile `node_modules/@local/dsh-video-preview`（链接或目录）。
3. 重启 DSH。然后本仓库可整体删除。

插件不写持久化数据、不改任何自带配置，删除后无残留。

## 8. 兼容性基线

- 实测 DSH `0.2.1-rc.2`（Desktop build commit `332895e0f7c9d4dbfb29729f5eb367fa263ff986`）。
- 依赖的上游公开契约（已核对内置包源码）：
  - `ctx.documentPreviews.register({ id, extensions, binaryExtensions, title, loading, wrap })`
  - `sidebar.right.tab.document` keyed 槽（`locale` 选项；body props：`content`、`resourceAddress`、
    `useTabInfo`、`t`）
  - `ctx.connection.fetch.register({ path, methods, requestBody, fetch })`
  - `ctx.workspaceFiles.stat/readBytes`、`ctx.sessions.get`、`ctx.sandboxPolicy.resolve`
- DSH 升级后若这些契约或 `UNVIEWABLE_BINARY_EXTENSIONS` 实现变化：先跑 `tests/`，
  再按第 7 节卸载。若上游开始内置视频渲染器，直接删除本插件即可，原有行为不受影响。
- 其他 DSH 版本/平台请先按第 6 节验证；上游契约不兼容时插件最多是**不激活**，
  不会破坏 DSH 原有功能（设置 → 插件里可重试或卸载）。

## 9. 已知限制

- 播放能力取决于 Electron/Chromium 自带解码器：H.264/AAC 的 mp4、webm 等常见格式可播；
  H.265/HEVC 以及 AVI / WMV / FLV / MKV 等未注册扩展名（保持原「不可预览」提示，
  可在工具栏用系统应用打开）。
- **Desktop 端超过 32 MiB 的视频可播放但无法拖动进度**（Electron 自定义协议媒体不可 seek，
  见第 2 节）；页面会显示提示条，可用工具栏在系统应用中打开以获得完整控制。
  HTTP(S) 网页端没有此限制。若上游 DSH 桌面壳改用可 seek 的媒体服务，或 Electron 修复该缺陷，
  此限制自然消失。
- 音量控件是否可用取决于视频是否有音轨；无音轨文件由 Chromium 禁用，属预期行为。
- 视频预览为只读；不做转码、截图、字幕等额外功能。

## English quick start

A local, additive DSH plugin that adds video playback to the right Sidebar document preview
(`mp4/m4v/webm/mov/ogv`). It registers a renderer through the public
`ctx.documentPreviews` API plus a keyed `sidebar.right.tab.document` body; no shipped DSH file
is modified. On HTTP(S) pages the player streams through an authenticated range route; on the
Desktop `dsh-app://app/` shell it plays complete bytes from a Blob URL (≤32 MiB) because Electron
custom-protocol media cannot seek ([electron#38749](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/38749)).

```bash
git clone https://github.com/chenyitao123/dsh-video-preview.git
# then from a DSH session:
# plugin_manager install_bundle target=<repo>/plugin
```

Tested with DSH `0.2.1-rc.2` (Web/Desktop compositions). Remove with
`plugin_manager remove_bundle @local/dsh-video-preview`.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
中文 · [English](./README.en.md)

# Watcher

[![ci](https://github.com/daha1216/dsh-watcher/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/daha1216/dsh-watcher/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

## 安装

### DSH Studio 桌面 App（推荐）

打开 **设置 → 插件 → 添加插件**，在“包名或地址”中输入：

```text
github:daha1216/dsh-watcher#v0.7.0
```

桌面端插件管理器负责 Desktop profile 和内置包管理器。本发布已提交 `lib/`；普通使用不需要 clone、构建或安装 DSHX。若应用提示刷新或重新打开，请按提示完成。

### Web CLI

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:daha1216/dsh-watcher#v0.7.0
```

这条官方 CLI 命令只写入 `web` profile，不能修改 Desktop App 的 profile。对于已经运行的 Web Host，请重新打开该 Host 一次，再刷新网页。

需要 DeepSeek Harness **0.1.7-rc.2**（`@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.7-rc.2`）。peer 范围 `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.1.8 || ^0.2.0-rc.1`：0.1.7-rc.1、0.1.7-rc.2 和 **0.2.0-rc.x** 都能装，开发与测试仍以 0.1.7-rc.2 为准。Node `^22.19.0` 或 `>=24`。

DeepSeek Harness Web 的只读插件。点会话标题栏里的眼睛，把 Session 收成一张能折叠的工作路径：这轮走了几步、跑了几次、花了多久；再展开某一步看并行分支、工具结果，或一条默认折着的推理记录。

它不往对话里塞消息，不编隐藏思维链，也不替代官方 Trajectory。

![从逐项切到归类：两次改 package.json 收成 ×2](docs/screenshots/switch-mode.gif)

![三轮都收着，留下阶段数、执行数和 tok/s](docs/screenshots/collapsed-turns.png)

![第三轮展开：并行步骤还在原来的 Step 里](docs/screenshots/overview.png)

![步骤 2：glob 和 grep 两项并行](docs/screenshots/parallel.png)

![归类：修改 package.json ×2，展开仍是步骤 5 和 6](docs/screenshots/grouped.png)

> 截图取自 0.6.2。此后版式又换了两轮：0.6.3 的命令栏，以及 0.7.0 的状态条、扁平用量读数与可折叠执行路径；截图待补。

![新版式设计对照（上：0.6.3；下：0.7.0 重构；设计稿，非实机截图）](docs/screenshots/panel-redesign.png)

归类只叠能证明相同的调用。两条不同的 bash 不会被捏在一起。模型阶段只显示供应商已经写进 Session 的可见 reasoning；没有记录就写未记录。

已经 clone 过的目录也可以（开发/本地测试）：

```sh
git clone https://github.com/daha1216/dsh-watcher.git
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-watcher
```

同样需要 pnpm，然后重新打开该 Web Host 并刷新页面。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-watcher
```

官方 CLI 只管理 `web` profile；Desktop App 请使用上面的应用内“添加插件”入口。

设置页和会话 HUD 的 Token 总数旁有 **估算费用**（不是「总价值」）。按模型的输入 / 输出 / 缓存桶对照 `pricing/models.yaml` 计价；缺行显示 **未知**，不会当成 $0。部分已知时主数字只显示已标价金额，未标价写在脚注。这是估算，不是账单。默认表含 DeepSeek、MiniMax、OpenAI、Anthropic、Gemini、Grok、GLM、Qwen 主流行，不联网。设置里打开的是当前生效价格表；保存只把改动过的行写入 `localStorage` 键 `dsh-watcher:pricing-override:v1`。欢迎对默认表提 PR。

交互约定在 [DESIGN.md](./DESIGN.md)。MIT。

## 本次更新（未发布，0.7.0）

- **面板做减法，路径成为主角。** 撤掉常驻的命令栏、路径工具栏与整块会话 HUD，只留三样：44px 状态条（状态点、状态词、当前动作，右侧搜索 / 用量 / 视图三个图标按钮）、26px 无边框指标线（轮次 · 步骤 · 执行数；Token · 估算成本 · 缓存命中；右侧实时 tok/s）、单行时间线。搜索与「全部 / 异常 / 等待」筛选收进搜索行，统计收进「用量与耗时」浮层，组织 / 展开 / 载入更早 / 载入全部 / 跳到最新收进「⋯」菜单。
- **时间线一行一条记录。** 轮次头 33px、阶段头 30px、记录行 26px；只有一个记录且没有模型阶段的 Step 直接展平，步骤号并入记录 meta，不再为单条记录多占一个头。耗时仍逐级可见（轮次总耗时、阶段跨度、记录耗时、tok/s），但去掉了阶段时长占比条。
- **代码层同步拆开。** 新建 `src/client/panel/`：`panel-model.ts` 放筛选投影、Step 展平、meta / 信号 / 簇文案等纯函数；`PanelHeader`、`MetricsStrip`、`SearchRow`、`ViewMenu`、`StatsPopover`、`PathTimeline`、`TurnSection`、`PhaseSection`、`OccurrenceRow` 各管一段；`Watcher.tsx` 只留状态与装配。`Overview.tsx` 删除（逻辑并入 `PhaseSection` / `TurnSection`），`Watcher.module.css` 从 1992 行裁到 989 行，只剩面板壳、检视器、模型阶段与拖拽手柄。
- **契约测试跟着结构改。** `presentation-contract` 断言三颗工具按钮与三个 `data-watcher-overlay`、唯一一个带 `flat` 的 `SessionInsights`、状态条 / 指标线的 divider 归属、展平行与簇折叠；新增 `tests/panel-model.test.mjs`。
- **结构与视觉重整（此前未发布）。** `Watcher.tsx` 从 2029 行降到 795 行；`Insights.tsx`（2142 行）拆成会话 HUD、设置页、检视器、概览、模型阶段、分析模块与六个 `insights-sections/` 文件。样式模块从三个变成五个，其中一个只放共享词表。
- **一套语义变量。** 所有样式模块改读 `src/client/ui/tokens.module.css` 的 `--ui-*` 别名层：十六进制色值归零，不再直接引用 `--dsw-static-*`，也不再保留 `var(--dsw-*, 回退值)` 写法。别名层作为 class 挂在每个客户端根元素上（跨文件 `composes` 在插件的 css-modules 构建里不生效），主题 token 仍靠继承下传。
- **能用宿主控件就用宿主控件。** 设置页的保存 / 刷新与数值上限改用 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-primitives` 的 `Button` 与 `Input`；组织 / 深度、统计范围、模型、时间范围四个开关换成新增的 `ui/SegmentedToggle`，视觉配方照抄宿主分段控件。它是有标签的 `role="group"` 切换按钮组，而不是宿主的 `SegmentedControl`：这些开关只改变同一内容的呈现方式，没有可供 `aria-controls` 指向的面板。
- **深度回到一个宿主阴影加一条描边。** 去掉顶部高光、接触 / 主 / 环境三层阴影与图表装饰光晕；悬停改用宿主填充和焦点环。
- **可访问性与可读性。** HUD 的洞察卡与会话表格行原本是可点击的 `div`、键盘不可达，现在是真正的按钮；说明性小字抬到宿主 11px 下限，小控件命中区扩大到 24px；热力图准星改为焦点环描边。
- **设置页不再在渲染路径里重算统计。** 聚合、分布与会话表格每次扫描只算一次，只有扫描结果或时间范围变化时才重算。
- **扫描失败不再伪装成空账本。** 失败会直接说明；首次扫描与「确实没有数据」区分开；被截断或跳过的会话在脚注里点名。
- **按工作分类上色保留在路径上。** 每个阶段仍有自己的色相，但只画在阶段标记点与它左侧 2px 边上；运行态、实时 tok/s 用宿主业务蓝，品牌墨色留给选中态。
- **检视器不再重复执行路径。** 保留头部、指标与「结果 / 输入 / 原始」三个 tab，新增记录步进器：「上一条 / 下一条」加 `记录 K/M` 位置，并接上方向键；切换记录不必退回路径。详情 tab 也补上了 `id` / `aria-controls` / `tabpanel` 语义。
- **Esc 分层。** 有记录打开时只关详情并把焦点还给路径；没有记录时才关面板。详情打开时方向键在记录间移动，输入框与可编辑区域内不拦截。
- **宽面板分栏。** 面板被拖宽到 980px 以上时，详情停靠在路径右侧而不是盖住它；更窄时仍是覆盖式抽屉。阈值用 `ResizeObserver` 量面板本身。
- **设置页分成四个 tab。** 「概览 / 趋势 / 会话 / 偏好」各管一段，时间范围控件在「偏好」页隐藏；下钻改为覆盖在页面上的对话框（背景遮罩、Esc 关闭、焦点还给打开它的卡片）。
- **会话账单。** 加搜索框与「显示更多会话」分页（每次 10 行），标题行保留排序控件，副标题补上总数。
- **清掉死样式。** 随旧面板删除的命令栏、工具栏、HUD、旧阶段 / 轮次样式与悬空选择器一并清掉；契约测试改为断言耗时与状态真正渲染的位置。

## 上次更新（0.6.3）

- **面板换成实心仪表盘。** 去掉毛玻璃：不透明底色、1px 描边、顶部高光与分层阴影；图表 tooltip 和计时卡统一到同一套表面变量。
- **顶栏改成两行命令栏。** 上行是状态行（圆点、状态、实时动作、跟随），下行是下沉的控制行（计数与历史加载、归类/深度切换）。轮次改成章节式排版；检视器从挤压列改成覆盖式右侧抽屉，展开时工作路径不再回流，面板宽度也不变。
- **阶段行压成单行。** 从 80–100px 的两行头压到 34px 一行（标记、箭头、标题与徽章、右对齐的步骤/执行/耗时），完整措辞保留在 aria-label；行底加 2px 时长占比条，一眼看出时间花在哪。同样的面板高度大约能多放 2.5 倍的行。
- **设置页与 HUD 统一视觉。** 四个等宽指标块、带语义色的洞察卡、去 emoji 的下钻面板，硬编码色值全部换成 dsw token 与 `color-mix`。
- **折叠内容不再占 DOM。** 收起的分支按需渲染，空闲面板不再每秒遍历历史子树；一轮里只有正在执行的阶段订阅 1Hz 时钟。
- **更快、更省内存。** 同一次折叠在真实 3,409 事件会话上快 37%（35.4ms → 22.1ms）且输出逐字节一致；面板关闭时不再折叠；长期驻留的合并结果与诊断集合都有上限。
- **兼容与工程化。** peer 范围放宽到 `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.1.8 || ^0.2.0-rc.1`；补上 typecheck / build / test 的 GitHub Actions。

## 0.6.1

- 在官方 DeepSeek Harness **0.1.7-rc.2** 上核对通过。`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 的 peer 仍是 `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.1.8`，安装期接受 `0.1.7-rc.1` 和 `0.1.7-rc.2`，不接受 `0.1.7-alpha.*`。
- 图标仍是 `IconChevronRightOutlineRegular`、`IconRefreshOutlineRegular`、`IconCheckOutlineRegular`、`IconCopyOutlineRegular`。rc.2 同样没有带尺寸后缀的旧导出。

## 0.6.0

- 对齐官方 DeepSeek Harness **0.1.7-rc.1**。`@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` 的 peer 改为 `>=0.1.7-rc.1 <0.1.8`，安装期接受 `0.1.7-rc.1`，不接受 `0.1.7-alpha.*`。
- 图标改为 `IconChevronRightOutlineRegular`、`IconRefreshOutlineRegular`、`IconCheckOutlineRegular`、`IconCopyOutlineRegular`。rc.1 删掉了带尺寸后缀的旧导出，没有别名。

## 0.5.0

- **面板能拖大。** 右边缘、下边缘和右下角把手都能拖；位置全程不动，最小只能缩回打开时的默认尺寸，不会小到放不下内容。
- **HUD 可折叠成一行。** 范围切换旁多了一个 `▾`，收起只留顶栏统计，选择会被记住。
- **"定位现场"真的到现场。** 现在会选中告警对应的具体失败步骤、直接打开检视器，而不是只滚到轮次标题。
- **连续失败不再刷屏。** 同一条失败链更新同一张卡片，标题带上 `第 N 轮`。

外加一串 0.4.5 的修复：检视器返回不再抢跟随、首次选范围不重复扫会话、投影状态不再存一份自身视图、计时面板文案改为"终端以外的工具"。

历史版本见 [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)。

## 从源码构建

日常安装不用这一步。改 TypeScript 后用 **pnpm** 重建已提交的 `lib/`：

```sh
pnpm install
pnpm test
node scripts/link-harness-dependencies.mjs /path/to/harness
pnpm build
```

`pnpm build` 需要能解析 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` peer 的本机 Harness 检出。装插件不要走这条路径。

冷会话的 Chat 数据尚未到达时，Watcher 显示等待提示，数据到达后再挂载面板。

# client-resume-button

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](./LICENSE)
[![DSH](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-%3E%3D0.2.0--rc.2-blue)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness)

给 DeepSeek Harness 的输入框加一个「继续」按钮：上一轮被中断后，点一下就能让模型接着把那一轮做完。

[English](./README.en.md) | 中文

---

## 效果

![preview](./docs/screenshot.png)

红圈处即「继续」按钮，位于模型选择器左侧。开始输入或添加附件时它收窄消失，清空后展开回来。

## 功能

按钮出现条件（需全部满足）：

- 上一轮以 `aborted`（用户按停止）、`interrupted`（崩溃）或 `error` 结束
- 输入框为空（无文字、无附件）
- 当前无轮次运行

点击后发送两条 plugin 来源的提示给模型：一条要求继续，一条提醒检查残留进程、不重做已完成步骤。

## 安装

```
插件页 → 「添加插件」→ 输入 client-resume-button → 安装 → 重启 DSH
```

命令行等价写法：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add client-resume-button
```

**装完必须重启 DSH**，浏览器端代码只在启动时加载。

<details>
<summary>其他安装方式</summary>

从 Git 仓库（需要能访问 `github.com`）：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add github:ddy-007/dsh-client-resume-button
```

若 `github.com` 不可达，可临时借助 `ghproxy.net` 这类第三方镜像转发。镜像只是绕开网络限制的便利手段，不是推荐路径——它会把安装流量经第三方转发，其供应链可信度未经本项目评估。优先用 npm 包或直连 GitHub。

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://ghproxy.net/https://github.com/ddy-007/dsh-client-resume-button.git
```

改源码时用 `link:`，不必每次重装，改完只需重启：

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop add "link:<仓库绝对路径>"
```

</details>

## 卸载

```sh
dsh plugin --profile desktop remove client-resume-button
```

## 验证

判断按钮该不该出现的是 `lib/projection.js`，它没有任何 import，因此测试不需要装依赖、不需要联网：

```sh
npm test          # 26 个断言
npm run record    # 每态一次折叠的运行记录
```

用例的事件形状取自真实会话日志，不是构造的近似值。CI 另跑 manifest 与打包内容检查。

## 限制

- **按钮位于模型选择器左侧**，不在主提交按钮旁。更近的 `conversation.input.activity` 槽位是 `single` 类型，已被语音输入插件占用，抢占会导致应用无法启动。
- **开始新一轮后按钮就消失**。中断标记会在下一次 `turn/start` 时清除——中断后只要又发了消息，无论内容是什么，都无法再「继续上一轮」。
- **不能恢复中断时的半截输出**。那部分内容从未写入日志，插件是新开一轮 turn 重做，而非续写原流。

## 兼容性

实测 DSH `0.2.0-rc.2`、`0.2.1-rc.2`。`dsh.engines.dsh` 声明 `>=0.2.0-rc.2 <0.3.0`，低于下界或达到 `0.3.0` 会被拒绝安装。

依赖以下内部约定，DSH 升级后可能失效：`turn/end` reason 枚举、`conversation.input.right` 槽位、`<hash>_primary` 类名、`agent.inbox.prepend` / `agent.steer`、`window.__ModuleLoader__.load`。

## 许可

MIT

# @dreamor/dsh-memvault Cordis plugin bridging [MemVault](../README.md) into [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`). The `dsh`/Cordis API surface it relies on (`ctx.systemPrompt.section()`, `session/event` payloads, `Plugin.Object` resolution) was verified against the actual `deepseek-harness` source, not secondhand docs. ## What it does - **Auto-injection**: keeps `memory://session-inject` cached and registers it as a system prompt section (`ctx.systemPrompt.section()`), refreshed eagerly at load and again on every `turn/end`. No agent tool call required. - **Auto-extraction**: on `turn/end` with `reason.kind === 'completed'`, calls MemVault's `notify_response` with **both** that turn's assistant text and the user's own turn text (`user/message` events with `source.kind === 'user'`) automatically. Passing the user's own words matters — MemVault's extractor signal words are first-person ("我偏好"/"我喜欢"), which match a user's own statement far more reliably than an assistant's restatement of it. If you only want the raw 16 MemVault tools exposed to the model (no auto-injection/auto-extraction), you don't need this package — dsh's own `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` does the same with zero code: each upstream server gets its own Cordis plugin instance via `cordis.patch.yml` (`transport: stdio`, `serverName: memvault`, `command: `). ## Install Prerequisites: a working `dsh` install (e.g. `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`) and the `memvault-proxy` binary reachable from `PATH` (or point `binaryPath` at one — see the override section below). Build, then install into a dsh profile from the repo's `dsh-plugin/` directory: ```bash cd dsh-plugin npm install npm run build # tsc --strict npx @deepseek-ai/dsh plugin --profile add "$PWD" ``` `dsh plugin add` runs the equivalent of `pnpm add` and appends the package to that profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` automatically — no manual edit of the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` is needed for a default install. The plugin ships a `cordis.patch.yml` that registers one `memvault` entry with the default config (`mode: spawn`, `embeddingProvider: native`, …). Verify the composed config, then start: ```bash npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --profile --dump-config # 组合后应只有一条 id: memvault 且字段正确 npx @deepseek-ai/dsh --port 0 # 实际启动方式以你的 dsh 用法为准 ``` At startup the plugin spawns `memvault-proxy` on port 3778 and probes `http://127.0.0.1:3778/health` until the server is ready. To confirm the injection actually lands: start a real conversation turn, then decompress the session log (`zstd -d ~/.dsh/sessions/.../session.jsonl.zstd`) and check that `request/header.data.header.system` contains the injected `[MUST]`/`[REF]` blocks. ### Overriding config (local development) To override a single field (e.g. point `binaryPath` at a locally built `memvault-proxy`), add a **bare-id override patch** to the profile's `cordis.patch.yml` and rewrite the whole `config` block — an override replaces the entire `config`, it does not merge per-field: ```yaml - id: memvault name: '@dreamor/dsh-memvault' config: mode: spawn db: '~/.memvault/data.db' port: 3778 binaryPath: /absolute/path/to/memvault-proxy embeddingProvider: native agentId: dsh injectOnAssemble: true extractOnTurnEnd: true ``` The `cordis.patch.yml` this plugin ships wraps its entry in `insert:` because the entry doesn't exist in any earlier layer. A bare `- id:` patch is an *override* that requires the id to already exist and errors with `patch: entry "memvault" not found` otherwise — an override patch must rewrite the whole `config` block, it never merges per-field. ## Config | Field | Default | Meaning | |---|---|---| | `mode` | `spawn` | `spawn` manages a `memvault-proxy` child process; `attach` connects to `url`. | | `db` | `~/.memvault/data.db` | Used when `mode: spawn`. | | `port` | `3778` | Used when `mode: spawn`. | | `url` | `''` | Used when `mode: attach`, e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:3778/mcp`. | | `binaryPath` | `''` (resolved from `PATH`) | Used when `mode: spawn`. | | `embeddingProvider` | `native` | Used when `mode: spawn` — forced as `MEMVAULT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER` in the child's env, so it can't accidentally inherit dsh's own `OPENAI_API_KEY`. | | `agentId` | `dsh` | Reported to MemVault on every call. | | `injectOnAssemble` | `true` | Toggle auto-injection. | | `extractOnTurnEnd` | `true` | Toggle auto-extraction. | ## Build ```bash npm install npm run build npm test ``` ## Status Builds clean (`tsc --strict`) against the real, npm-published `@deepseek-ai/cordis@4.0.4`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-system-prompt@0.2.0-rc.2`, `@deepseek-ai/dsh-session@0.2.0-rc.2`, and `@deepseek-ai/dsh-llm@0.2.0-rc.2` packages (not mocks — see `src/index.smoke.test.ts`, which mounts the plugin on a real `Context` alongside the real `SystemPrompt` service and asserts `ctx.systemPrompt.assemble()` actually contains the injected section). **Fully verified end to end against a real `dsh` install** (`npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web`, v0.1.0-rc.6). Four real bugs were found and fixed in the course of the verification: 1. `cordis.patch.yml` insert vs. override patch semantics (a bare `id` patch requires the id to already exist). 2. `memvault-proxy` inheriting a stray `OPENAI_API_KEY` from dsh's own process env, plus a stale (pre-`native`-embedding) local binary. 3. The eager injection-cache refresh at `apply()` time racing `memvault-proxy`'s own startup (`fetch failed`). 4. `mcp-client.ts` permanently caching a *failed* connection attempt — `connected ??= (...)` memoized on the first (raced, failing) call, so every later call kept re-rejecting forever, never retrying even after the proxy came up. With all four fixed, a real conversation turn's session log (`~/.dsh/sessions/.../session.jsonl.zstd`, decompressed with `zstd -d`) shows the actual `request/header.data.header.system` text containing MemVault's injected `[MUST]`/`[REF]` memories, and a direct `notify_response` call against the running `memvault-proxy` moved MemVault's memory count from 8 to 10 (new preference/fact memories actually saved to Inbox). A follow-up round extended `notify_response` to also extract from the user's own turn text — MemVault's extractor signal words are first-person, so a user's own statement ("我偏好用 tabs") matches far more reliably than an assistant's restatement of it ("你偏好用 tabs" used to be silently rejected; the signal-word list was also extended with second/third-person mirrors). Verified against the real running `memvault-proxy`: memory count went from 10 to 13 across three scenarios, with `source:user`/`source:assistant` tags on the results. DSH 0.2 compatibility has also been checked with `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*@0.2.0-rc.2` and a real `dsh@0.2.0-rc.2` `plugin add` / `--dump-config` run; the plugin keeps its wildcard peer range so DSH 0.1 installs remain usable.
# MemVault ### The Shared Memory Layer for Every AI Agent You Run > Not "agent learns to search memory" — memory finds the agent. **MCP Native  ·  Hybrid Retrieval  ·  Auto-Injection  ·  Zero-Config Sync** **Open Source  ·  Self-Hosted  ·  Private  ·  MIT Licensed** [![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/memvault-cli.svg?style=flat-square)](https://crates.io/crates/memvault-cli) [![GitHub Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/dreamor/memvault?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/dreamor/memvault/releases) [![CI](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/dreamor/memvault/ci.yml?style=flat-square&branch=master)](https://github.com/dreamor/memvault/actions) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/Rust-stable-orange.svg?style=flat-square)](https://www.rust-lang.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP-compatible-blue.svg?style=flat-square)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-beta-yellow.svg?style=flat-square)](#project-status) **English**  ·  [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)
If MemVault solves a real problem for you, a star helps others find it. **[⭐ Star on GitHub](https://github.com/dreamor/memvault)**  ·  **[Report Bug](https://github.com/dreamor/memvault/issues/new)**
```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dreamor/memvault/master/scripts/install.sh | bash ```
--- Every AI agent session starts from scratch. Claude Desktop doesn't know what Cursor just learned. DeepSeek Harness (dsh) doesn't know what you told Claude Code yesterday. Whatever agent you're running — international or domestic, IDE plugin or CLI harness — it forgets your preferences every time you start a new conversation. You've been manually repeating context — project conventions, personal preferences, past decisions — across agents that should already know. This isn't a limitation of the models. It's a missing infrastructure layer. MemVault is that layer. A lightweight, self-hosted memory router that sits between your agents and their context. It speaks plain MCP — no MemVault-specific SDK, no per-agent API integration. **Any MCP-compatible agent, from any vendor, automatically shares the same persistent memory the moment it connects.** **Who it's for:** - **Anyone running an MCP-capable agent** — Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Continue, DeepSeek Harness (dsh), or any other MCP client, domestic or international — who wants preferences, project context, and past decisions to persist across sessions without repeating yourself - **Multi-agent power users** running several of the above side by side, on different models, from different vendors — all sharing the same memory without configuration - **Platform teams** deploying AI-assisted workflows where consistency matters across a mixed agent fleet: code review conventions, architecture decisions, project-specific preferences - **Anyone tired of telling their AI the same thing twice** — MemVault works the way your brain should: you say it once, it's there when you need it, no matter which agent is asking **[Quick Start](#quick-start)**  ·  **[How It Works](#how-it-works)**  ·  **[What MemVault Gives You](#what-memvault-gives-you)**  ·  **[Why MemVault](#why-memvault)**  ·  **[MCP Server](#mcp-server)**  ·  **[CLI Reference](#cli-reference)**  ·  **[Integrations](#integrations)**  ·  **[Architecture](#architecture)**  ·  **[Project Status](#project-status)**  ·  **[Testing](#testing)**  ·  **[Documentation](#documentation)**  ·  **[Contributing](#contributing)**  ·  **[License](#license)** --- ## Quick Start Don't install MemVault by hand — paste this one prompt into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, dsh, or any other MCP-capable agent. It points the agent at a machine-readable install guide, so the agent does the whole setup itself: ```text Install MemVault as your long-term memory and wire it into this agent. Fetch and follow https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dreamor/memvault/master/docs/AGENT-INSTALL.md — install the binaries, register MemVault as an MCP server for this host, and verify recall works. Then keep saving my preferences, project decisions, and lessons from each session so my next agent starts with them instead of from scratch. ``` Or install manually: ```bash # Install (Linux / macOS): official script, auto-verifies SHA-256 curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/dreamor/memvault/master/scripts/install.sh | bash export PATH="$HOME/.memvault/bin:$PATH" # Windows (PowerShell): # powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install.ps1 # Homebrew (Apple Silicon): # brew install dreamor/tap/memvault # Or from crates.io: # cargo install memvault-cli memvault-mcp # The installers auto-start the local REST backend (host of the Web # Dashboard). Open it, or start it on demand: memvault-cli dashboard # Save a MUST-level preference (injected as instruction, agent must follow) memvault-cli save --content "User prefers Python" --priority MUST --type preference \ --instruction "Use Python for code, not Java" --tags "coding,python" # Search across all memory (hybrid: keyword + semantic when embedding is enabled) memvault-cli search --query "Python" # See what context gets injected when a specific agent connects memvault-cli session-start --agent-id claude-desktop --context "Help me write code" # Extract structured memories from free text memvault-cli extract --text "I prefer dark mode. Our project uses Rust." --save # Auto-generate agent instruction files from memory memvault-cli sync # All in one: dedup, decay, archive stale memories memvault-cli dedup && memvault-cli decay ``` > **System requirements:** > - **Prebuilt Linux binaries** (install script / GitHub release): glibc ≥ 2.38 + GLIBCXX_3.4.31 (GCC 13-era runtime — Ubuntu 24.04+ / Fedora 39+ / Arch; `memvault-proxy` additionally wants glibc ≥ 2.39). TLS is rustls, so no OpenSSL dependency. Ubuntu 22.04 / RHEL or EL8/EL9 users: use the Docker image (`dreamor/memvault`) or build from source. > - **Building from source** (`cargo install` / `cargo build`): links fastembed's prebuilt ONNX Runtime static library and needs a GCC 13-class toolchain. Older toolchains (e.g. GCC 8, CentOS 7/8-era libstdc++) fail at link time with missing C++20/23 stdlib symbols (`std::format`, `std::to_chars`). macOS / Windows (MSVC) / Homebrew / Docker are unaffected. **Verify your install in 5 seconds:** ```bash memvault-cli --version # memvault 0.6.0 # sanity check: list saved memories (verifies DB is healthy) memvault-cli list ``` ### Local Ollama Demo (Zero Cost, Stays on Your Machine) MemVault is plug-and-play with a local Ollama: unconfigured LLM extraction (full-text understanding / failure reflection / relation extraction) auto-detects a local Ollama; embeddings use the local model with the `ollama` or `auto` provider. ```bash # 1. Install and start Ollama brew install ollama && brew services start ollama # or the official installer # 2. Pull models ollama pull nomic-embed-text # embeddings, 768-dim (default for ollama/auto) ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct # chat: LLM extraction/reflection (default qwen2.5:7b, use 3b on small machines) # 3. (Optional) Pin the providers explicitly — persist them in ~/.memvault/.env # (shell exports also work — env vars take precedence over the file — but the file survives reboots) mkdir -p ~/.memvault cat >> ~/.memvault/.env <<'EOF' MEMVAULT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=ollama MEMVAULT_LLM_EXTRACTION_PROVIDER=ollama MEMVAULT_LLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL=qwen2.5:3b-instruct EOF # 4. Verify memvault-cli status # Embedding provider: configured and reachable memvault-cli save --content "Build server IP is 10.20.30.40" # output (embedded int8) memvault-cli outcome --task "Deploy trading service" --status failure --cause "Disk space insufficient" --task-type deploy # → Lesson (Llm): ... means failure reflection ran through the local LLM (not the rule-based fallback) ``` With no configuration at all (neither env vars nor `~/.memvault/.env`), LLM extraction auto-detects a local Ollama and enables itself (default model `qwen2.5:7b`; pull it in advance with `ollama pull qwen2.5:7b`, or point `MEMVAULT_LLM_EXTRACTION_MODEL` at an installed model). Embeddings still default to the in-process native embedder; set `MEMVAULT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=auto` in `~/.memvault/.env` to prefer Ollama and fall back to native when it isn't running. The native model's first launch downloads the weights from HuggingFace **silently in the background** — the server/dashboard come up immediately and hot-swap to semantic search once the download finishes, so a fresh install never blocks on it (set `MEMVAULT_EMBEDDING_PROVIDER=none` to run pure keyword and skip the download). --- ## How It Works MemVault is a pipeline, not a single script. Every stage below is a shipping module: ``` Agent connects (MCP stdio/SSE) │ ▼ ┌───────────────────┐ │ Agent Router │ ← match agent type/tag → filter relevant memory │ (Agent Registry) │ └────────┬──────────┘ │ ▼ ┌───────────────────┐ │ Memory Retrieval │ ← keyword (BM25) + vector (embedding) + RRF fusion │ (3 search modes) │ synonym expansion · scoring · soft filtering └────────┬──────────┘ │ ▼ ┌───────────────────┐ │ Auto-Injection │ ← MUST-level → instruction prompt │ │ REFERENCE → context resource │ │ NORMAL → search result └────────┬──────────┘ │ ▼ Agent receives context ──→ makes better decisions ``` - **Storage:** SQLite with bundled FTS5 (full-text search); embeddings stored int8-quantized (~1/4 the size of f32 at near-identical ranking quality, legacy f32 rows still readable) - **Retrieval:** BM25 keyword search over FTS5 with CJK bigram tokenization (Chinese two-character words match correctly) and tiered match fallback (strict → relaxed unigram → synonym OR; relaxations are reported, never silent), local-first embedding (in-process native by default — switch to local Ollama or any OpenAI-compatible model), RRF fusion with per-result recall provenance (`kw#2`/`vec#5`), synonym expansion, relevance scoring, soft intent filtering - **Pipeline:** Automatic entity extraction, delta-write on save (near-duplicates skipped, similar memories absorb only the residual), semantic deduplication, time-based decay, archive of stale memories - **Sync:** Zero-invasion file generation — `memvault-cli sync` produces CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, etc. directly from database contents --- ## What MemVault Gives You - **Auto-Injected Context:** Session start automatically pulls relevant memory by agent identity — MUST-level rules land as instructions, not just chat history - **Hybrid Retrieval:** BM25 + vector + RRF fusion with synonym expansion, relevance scoring, and per-result provenance (which path recalled each memory, at what rank) — available via CLI, MCP tool, and REST API - **Explainable Injection:** every candidate dropped on the way into an agent's context is recorded with a reason (budget, caps, intent/type penalties) — "why didn't the agent get this memory?" always has an answer - **MUST Enforcement:** MUST-priority memories are never filtered or truncated. Always in context, always obeyed — trust comes from provenance (human-authored/reviewed), with an opt-in fallback for memories independently corroborated by multiple identity-verified agents (`MEMVAULT_CORROBORATION_GATE`), so a single spoofed/compromised agent can't unilaterally inject a binding MUST - **Multi-Agent Awareness:** Agent Registry with type/tag-based soft filtering (score demotion, not hard exclusion) - **`agent_id` Is Provenance, Not a Filter:** retrieval never filters by `agent_id` — the field only records which agent wrote a memory (`source_agent`). Every agent searches the same shared corpus; per-agent differences apply only at injection time (type/tag soft scoring via `agents.yaml` `inject_rules`) - **MCP Proxy:** Transparent proxy that injects memory into ANY upstream MCP server's responses — zero client changes - **Compliance Tracking:** `inject_session_id` traces what was injected and measures follow-through rate - **Cross-Platform:** CLI + MCP Server (stdio & SSE) + Web Dashboard (browser) + Obsidian Plugin - **Zero-Invasion Sync:** Generate AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md from memory — no per-agent config files to edit - **Contextual Extraction, Local-First:** Rule-based keyword extraction by default; optionally understands a full user+assistant exchange via an LLM, auto-detecting a local Ollama for free before ever touching a remote API - **History & Rollback:** Every update/delete is snapshotted into `memory_history` — `memvault-cli checkpoints` + `memvault-cli restore` roll one memory back without touching the rest - **Self-Diagnostics:** `memvault-cli status` reports exactly which features are degraded when no embedding provider is configured, plus a schema fingerprint (migration version + checksum) for cross-database comparison - **Episodic Memory:** `record_outcome` records task results; failures are distilled into lessons and auto-injected next time (REFERENCE → MUST only with human approval), so the same trap isn't hit twice - **Procedural Skill Activation:** skills whose `trigger` matches intent are injected as structured `[SKILL]` blocks with success-rate stats (shown after ≥3 runs); failures flag the skill for revision (`version++` on human edit), repeated successes auto-draft new skills into the review inbox - **Semantic Knowledge Links:** lightweight relation triples, repeated facts consolidated into a linked semantic fact with provenance, and superseded facts archived (never re-injected, still listable & restorable) - **Team Shared Pool & SOP Import:** memories marked `shared` are injected into every session (capped at 20); Markdown SOPs can be batch-imported as verifiable skills - **Delta-Write on Save:** every save is checked against its namespace first — near-duplicates are skipped, similar memories absorb only the *residual* (what's genuinely new) and get their strength refreshed, so the library converges instead of accumulating near-copies; `--force` / `force_insert` bypasses - **Task-Level Evaluation:** `memvault-cli bench` samples your own failure history (episodes that distilled a lesson) and measures lesson retrieval/injection rates — and with `--judge`, an LLM scores "plan without vs. with memory" against the known failure cause, so you see *task-success* lift, not just retrieval recall - **Two-Phase Injection (never blocks):** MUST rules resolve deterministically with zero embedding calls and are served immediately; the semantic pipeline prefetches in the background and lands within a short window (250ms) — if it doesn't, the deterministic baseline is served and the request moves on (two-phase design) - **Conversation-N-Gram Retrieval:** retrieval keys are conditioned on the recent turn window, weighted by recency so the current focus dominates — not a single flat query - **Single Canonical Injection Channel:** per-agent `inject_channel` (`mcp` / `proxy` / `sync` in `agents.yaml`) restricts automatic injection to one delivery path, so the same memory is never sent to the same agent twice - **Data You Own:** Single SQLite file. Full export/import. No cloud dependency. Your data, your machine. --- ## Why MemVault Looking for a **self-hosted alternative to Mem0, Zep, or Letta/MemGPT**? Those are hosted APIs or Python frameworks tied to one SDK. MemVault ships as a single Rust binary with no hosted service and no vendor lock-in, speaks plain MCP instead of a proprietary SDK, and shares one memory store across every agent you run — Claude Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, dsh — not just one. | Feature | Plain CLAUDE.md | Vector DB + RAG | **MemVault** | |---|---|---|---| | **Context injection** | Manual edits | Query-time only | Auto on session start | | **Multi-agent sharing** | Copy-paste | Separate indexes | Single shared store | | **MUST enforcement** | None | None | Instruction-layer injection | | **Search modes** | File grep | Embedding only | BM25 + Vector + Hybrid | | **Synonym expansion** | No | No | Built-in | | **Deduplication** | No | No | Semantic dedup pipeline | | **Write-time delta merge** | No | No | Near-dupes skip, similar absorb the residual at save | | **Task-level evaluation** | None | Recall metrics only | `bench`: with-vs-without-memory task success delta | | **Decay / archival** | No | No | Time-based + auto archive | | **Memory extraction** | Manual | N/A | Rule-based by default; optional local-first LLM extraction | | **MCP native** | No | No | stdio + SSE + Proxy | | **Agent differentiation** | Global file | Query filter | Type/tag registry | | **Compliance tracking** | None | None | inject_session_id + rate | | **Self-hosted** | Yes | Varies | Single binary, no cloud | MemVault complements your existing agent setup rather than replacing it. Keep your LLM, your IDE, and your workflow exactly as they are. MemVault adds the memory layer underneath. --- ## MCP Server > Tier-1 agents (Claude Code, OpenCode, dsh, Gemini CLI, Codex) have one-command plugin installs — see [Installing into your agents](#installing-into-your-agents) first. Everything below is the universal fallback for any other MCP client. ### stdio (any standard MCP client) MemVault speaks plain MCP stdio — the same `mcpServers` JSON works verbatim in Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, Continue, and any other client that reads this format: ```json { "mcpServers": { "memvault": { "command": "/path/to/memvault-mcp", "args": ["--db", "~/.memvault/data.db"], "env": { "OPENAI_API_KEY": "sk-..." } } } } ``` A couple of clients use their own one-liner instead of hand-editing JSON: ```bash # Claude Code claude mcp add memvault /path/to/memvault-mcp -- --db ~/.memvault/data.db ``` **DeepSeek Harness (dsh)** — a domestic (China) agent harness — gets deeper treatment than a generic stdio config: a native Cordis plugin (`dsh-plugin/`) that auto-injects memory into the system prompt and auto-extracts at turn end, with no per-turn cooperation required from the agent. See [docs/INSTALL.md §2.5](docs/INSTALL.md#25-deepseek-harness-dsh) for both the zero-code MCP route and the deep-integration plugin. Other MCP-compatible agents — international or domestic, IDE plugin or CLI harness — should work the same way: any client implementing standard MCP stdio/SSE can connect without MemVault-side changes. The ones above are the ones we've actually verified; if you get MemVault working with another one, a PR to this list is welcome. ### SSE (multi-client, network-accessible) ```bash memvault-mcp --transport sse --port 3777 # Clients connect at http://127.0.0.1:3777/mcp ``` SSE features: multi-client simultaneous connections, auto-triggered embedding backfill on initialization, HTTP remote access. > **Note:** `--transport sse` only mounts the MCP-over-HTTP endpoint (`/mcp`) — it does **not** expose the REST API (`/api/*`). The Web Dashboard is served by the REST backend (`memvault-mcp --transport http --serve-web `), and the Obsidian plugin also uses the REST API and requires `--transport http` instead. See [docs/INSTALL.md §2.6](docs/INSTALL.md#26-rest-apiobsidian-客户端专用). ### 19 MCP Tools | Tool | Description | |------|-------------| | `save_memory` | Save with auto-embedding; delta-write by default (near-dupes skip, similar merge) — `force_insert` to bypass | | `record_outcome` | Record a task outcome (episodic memory); failures reflect into lessons | | `import_skills` | Import skills from a Markdown SOP (headings → skills, list items → steps) | | `search_memory` | Keyword / semantic / hybrid | | `session_start` | Agent-aware context injection; honors the agent's `inject_channel` (skips with an explanation when another channel is canonical) | | `review_memory` | Approve / reject / edit | | `delete_memory` | Remove a memory (soft delete — restorable via `restore`) | | `forget_memory` | Permanently erase one memory or a criteria-matched bulk set (GDPR-style, irreversible);
