evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-swarm-board The swarm board as a page of a DSH site. A plugin for [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness). - **`/board/`**: the board page (`wolffia/v8.html`, read once when DSH starts). - **`/board/data/.js`**: board data, read from the data directory on every request. Only `index.js`, `p.js` (a acme project) and `p--.js` (another org's project) are served. Any other name, including `..`, gets 404. - **`POST /board/api/epic/go`** `{url, auto_merge?}`, **`api/epic/rego`** `{url}`, **`api/epic/automerge`** `{url, on}`, **`api/status`** `{project, url, status}`: release, re-release, auto-merge on/off, and move a card (lib/actions.js). These follow the same rules as Wolffia's host API, but use the site's `gh`. Comments say 「由 站台看板（）…」. Success returns `200 {ok:true, by, already?, auto_merge?, on?, state?}`, where `by` is the site's host name. Errors return `400/502 {error}`. Each route takes `application/json` only, rejects other sites' `Origin`, and caps the body at 4KB. `api/status` only takes projects listed in `projects`; `project` is the number (`2`, acme) or `"org/number"` (`"acme/1"`), and the Status field is changed in that project's own org. Without a logged-in `gh`, every route answers `409`. After a success, the plugin re-fetches that project's board data. - **`GET /board/api/projects/available`**: the projects the board can add (「＋ 加入 project…」). The site's `gh` lists, by GraphQL (it has no `gh project` command), the projects of the logged-in user and of every org they belong to. Only open projects are listed, most cards first: `{github:true, projects:[{owner, number, title, items, added}]}`, where `items` is the card count and `added` means the project is already on the board. The list is cached for 10 minutes; `added` is always current. Without a logged-in `gh` the answer is `{github:false}`. - **`POST /board/api/projects/add`** `{owner, number}`: adds one of those projects. The plugin asks GitHub again and refuses (`400`) anything that is not an open project of the user or their orgs, whatever the page sent. It appends the project to `projects.json` (all other entries stay), fetches it once right away, and returns `200 {ok:true, key, already, fetched, title, index}`, where `index` is the new `data/index.js` (`window.PROJECT_INDEX`). Adding a project that is already there is not an error (`already:true`). The project then joins every later fetch round and `api/status`. Same request rules as the other `POST` routes (JSON only, same origin, 4KB, `409` without `gh`). - **📋 看板** button: fixed at the bottom right of the DSH Web client. It opens `/board/` in a new tab. Every response carries `cache-control: no-store` and `x-content-type-options: nosniff`. ## Install You need: - DSH with the web profile (tested against the same DSH as `dsh-share-room`); - Node.js 22 or later. Steps: 1. Install it into your DSH web profile: ```bash dsh plugin --profile web add ./wolffia/site-plugin ``` DSH adds it to the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles` for you, and its `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `swarm-board` plugin. 2. Put the board data in the data directory (default `$DSH_HOME/swarm-board/data`): `index.js` and one `p.js` (or `p--.js`) per project. 3. Restart DSH. **📋 看板** appears at the bottom right. To update, run `dsh plugin --profile web update dsh-swarm-board`. To uninstall, run `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-swarm-board`. Where things live: - Host routes: one `webServer` prefix route, `/board`. - The button: `lib/launcher.js`, loaded by the DSH Web client as this package's `./client` bundle (`dsh.client` in `package.json`). The same file is served at `/board/_/launcher.js`. - **`/board` is not public.** It stays behind the site login. If a site-wide login gate sits in front of DSH (for example `@summersec/dsh-web-auth`), do **not** add `/board` to its public prefixes. Only `/share` (dsh-share-room guests) belongs there. ### Config Restate `swarm-board` in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`: ```yaml - id: swarm-board name: 'dsh-swarm-board' config: dataDir: /srv/swarm-board/data # default: $DSH_HOME/swarm-board/data html: /srv/swarm-board/v8.html # default: ../v8.html next to this package projects: [3, "acme/1"] # projects to fetch; also the only ones api/status may change siteName: board.example.com # `by` in action responses and comments; default: os.hostname() org: acme # project owner for api/status when the board data has none yet ``` Projects added from the board (「＋ 加入 project…」) are written to `projects.json`, one level above `dataDir`. On start the plugin uses `config.projects` plus every entry of that file, so added projects survive a restart. `projects` entries: - an integer `N` is the default org's project N (as before): data file `p.js`, board URL `/board/?p=N`; - a string `"org/N"` is project N of that org, e.g. `"acme/1"`: data file `p-acme-1.js`, board URL `/board/?p=acme/1`. `"acme/N"` is the same as `N`. Org names are compared case-insensitively. Fetching, `api/status` and 運行中 (`/board/api/running`) each use the project's own org. `data/index.js` lists every project with `num`, `owner` and `key` (the entry above); `?p=` selects by `key`. ## Development ```bash cd wolffia/site-plugin node --test test/*.test.js ``` The tests use a fake ctx and fake req/res. They need no DSH. ### 「分析」的對話開在哪裡 新的「分析」對話用 `session.create` 的 `cwd` 開在站台的工作區：設定 `thinkCwd` 給的目錄；沒設就用 `HOME` 環境變數（站台裡是 `/home/dsh/workspace`）；連 `HOME` 都沒有就不帶 `cwd`（DSH 預設）。外掛不再自己建立 `$DSH_HOME/swarm-board/think` 工作區。 要放進側欄的分組（DSH Workspace）時，設定 `thinkWorkspace: <目錄>`，外掛才會在那個目錄建 Workspace（`thinkWorkspaceTitle` 改名稱，預設「📊 看板分析」）。沒給目錄就不建。 已經記在 `sessions.json` 的對話照舊續用，不會搬動。 ```yaml thinkCwd: /home/dsh/workspace # default: $HOME thinkWorkspace: /srv/board-think # optional; only then a DSH Workspace is created ``` ### 站台層級的 `epic` skill 外掛內附 `skills/epic/`：`SKILL.md`、`templates/epic.md`、`templates/sub-issue.md`，和只支援 `--file` 的離線 lint（`lint/epic_lint.py`＋`lint/epiclib/`，不需要 GitHub）。DSH 啟動時外掛把它複製到 `$DSH_HOME/skills/epic/`：目錄不存在、或內容和外掛版本不同時才寫，寫入先放暫存目錄再改名。設定 `skillsDir` 可改目標的 skills 目錄（預設 `$DSH_HOME/skills`）。 分析對話的提示寫「需要開 EPIC 時，用 `epic` skill」，不再指向 swarm repo 的路徑。 ```bash cd $DSH_HOME/skills/epic/lint python3 epic_lint.py --file <草稿> --labels by:swarm # 0 通過；1 不通過；2 參數錯誤 ``` `skills/epic/` 是 swarm repo 的 `docs/skills/epic/SKILL.md`、`docs/templates/`、`scheduler/epiclib/{lint,criteria}.py` 的站台版；那邊改了規則要同步過來（`scheduler/tests/epic/test_skill_bundle.py` 會檢查內附的 lint 能獨立跑）。 ### 每日聚合 每日聚合（`digestEveryMs`，預設一天）每一輪要跑之前先看 `gh auth status`：站台的 `gh` 沒登入就跳過這一輪、記一行 log，下一輪再看。 # Swarm [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | English [![CI](https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/towNingtek/swarm)](https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm/releases) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) An AI office you can host yourself, run by a **swarm**: AI agents take the issues of an EPIC in parallel, a judge accepts their work only when its acceptance criteria pass, and people decide and accept. You run one platform; each customer you invite gets an isolated [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) site that already holds an office template: companies, AI staff roles, schedules and a place for their own keys. ![The operator creates a customer and sends an invite; the customer activates, the site gets built, and they work with the AI in their own site](docs/media/demo.gif) Full video with captions: [docs/media/demo.mp4](docs/media/demo.mp4). The demo runs on a throwaway install with a scripted model, so the AI's replies are canned. > The UI text is currently in Traditional Chinese. ## How the swarm works Swarm turns a goal into **an EPIC of small issues**, hands each issue to an AI agent, and lets the agents work **in parallel**. A result is accepted only when the issue's **executable acceptance criteria** pass, run by a separate judge. People define the goal, release the work and accept the result; they do not need to watch it. Source: [`docs/diagrams/swarm-flow.en.mmd`](docs/diagrams/swarm-flow.en.mmd) | Stage | Who | Gate | |-------|-----|------| | ① Define | Person + `epic` skill | No issue without a testable "done"; every criterion is run first and must fail today; drafts must pass `epic_lint` | | ② Release | Person | Adding `swarm:go` freezes the criteria | | ③ Build and judge | Agents + runner | Each agent works in its own worktree, limited to the files its issue lists; issues on the same file are chained; the runner executes the criteria verbatim and counts only exit codes | | ④ Accept | Person | Review the EPIC pull request (low-risk EPICs may auto-merge); a closing summary feeds the monthly report | ![The board (demo data): planets are open issues on rings by status; clusters are EPICs with their completion arc; red glow means an issue is stuck](docs/media/30-board.png) Every site has the **Wolffia board** at `/board/`: a live view of a GitHub Project where you drag cards to change status, release EPICs, add projects from any org you can see, and ask **📊 Analyse** — the site's own AI reads the board and answers. See [`swarm/`](swarm/) and [`plugins/swarm-board/`](plugins/swarm-board/). ## What it does - **Invite-only sites.** In the admin console you create a customer, pick an office template, set a monthly model quota and send a single-use invite link. The customer picks their own username and password. - **One container per customer.** The platform builds the site by itself: a DSH container with its own login, data and workspace, an nginx route and (optionally) a DNS record. Deleting the customer removes all of it. - **Onboarding page with a setup copilot.** The customer sees setup progress and the site build live. The copilot explains the next step from what the platform actually recorded, and does not make up progress. - **Into the site without a second password.** **Open my site** hands the signed-in customer over with a single-use ticket. - **The platform's model key never enters a site.** Each site gets its own starter key, which only works against the platform's relay. The relay checks that key and the site's monthly budget, then forwards the call with the platform key. - **An office ready on first visit.** The workspace starts with the office template (an `AGENTS.md`, a getting-started guide, a place for companies). Customers can add their own model keys later. - **Conversation sharing.** [dsh-share-room](https://github.com/yillkid/dsh-share-room) is installed in every site, so a customer can invite guests into a conversation. - **Operator view.** One page lists every customer with their site, quota policy and template. When a customer asks for a human, the operator answers from the same console. ## Screenshots | Operator | Customer | |---|---| | ![Operator overview: every site, its usage, last run and what needs attention; 📊 board and site buttons on each card](docs/media/20-admin-overview.png) | ![Customer overview: own site, usage, recent runs, one-click board](docs/media/21-customer-overview.png) | | ![Activating an account from the invite link](docs/media/04-activate.png) | ![Customer settings: setup progress and the site password](docs/media/22-customer-settings.png) | | ![The single-use invite link (masked here)](docs/media/03-admin-invite.png) | ![The onboarding page with the site ready](docs/media/06-site-ready.png) | Inside the customer's own site: the reply comes through the platform relay, and the usage counts toward the monthly quota. ![Working with the AI inside the customer's own site](docs/media/09-site-chat.png) ## How it fits together Source: [`docs/diagrams/architecture.en.mmd`](docs/diagrams/architecture.en.mmd) Each site sits on an isolated Docker network. The relay is the only host port it can reach: no other host ports, private networks or cloud metadata. The platform never runs `sudo`. Two small root units do the privileged work, one for the firewall and one that applies nginx configs. Details: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) and [docs/security.md](docs/security.md). ## Before you run it - **Use a host dedicated to Swarm.** The platform user is in the `docker` group, which is equivalent to root. - **Containers are not VMs.** All customers share one kernel and one Docker daemon. DSH's in-site sandbox does not work in a container, so the container, network and firewall are the only containment. - **Sites can reach the internet.** A customer's AI can send that customer's data anywhere. - **You pay for the starter model.** Every site's starter calls go through your gateway on your key. Monthly caps are enforced, but token counts are estimates. - **TLS is yours.** Nothing here terminates TLS. Put certbot, a load balancer or a tunnel in front. The full list is under [Known limits](docs/security.md#known-limits). ## Install You need a Linux host (Ubuntu 22.04 or similar) with Docker 24+, nginx and Python 3.10+, about 2 GB of disk for the site image, and an OpenAI-compatible model gateway (for example LiteLLM). Point `platform.` and `*.` at the host. ```sh sudo git clone https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm /opt/swarm cd /opt/swarm sudo python3 -m venv .venv && sudo .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt sudo docker build -f site/Dockerfile -t swarm-site:latest . sudo deploy/install.sh sudo editor /etc/swarm/platform.env # domain, origins, model gateway sudo editor /etc/swarm/secrets/model-key sudo cp deploy/nginx/swarm-platform.conf.example /etc/nginx/conf.d/swarm-platform.conf sudo editor /etc/nginx/conf.d/swarm-platform.conf && sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx sudo deploy/install.sh --start ``` Then open `https://platform./admin` and sign in with the password in `/etc/swarm/secrets/admin-password`. The rest of the settings, logs and the first customer are covered in [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md). The whole install is tested from scratch in a throwaway container: `bash deploy/tests/clean-install/run.sh`. ## Repository | Path | What it is | |---|---| | [`platform/`](platform/) | The platform, the admin console and the site model relay | | [`site/`](site/) | The site engine and the DSH site image | | [`office-template/`](office-template/) | The office every new site starts with | | [`plugins/`](plugins/) | DSH plugins kept here: branding, and the board (Wolffia) with the `epic` skill | | [`swarm/`](swarm/) | The swarm orchestrator: agents, the judge, autostart, summaries and reports | | [`deploy/`](deploy/) | Install on one host with systemd, Docker and nginx | | [`demo/`](demo/) | The scripted model and recording scripts behind the demo above | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Architecture, security model, HTTP API, design records, swarm contracts | ## Development ```sh bash scripts/test.sh # every suite; Python 3.10+, Node 22 ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how issues are written here (EPICs with executable acceptance criteria) and what a pull request needs. The platform is Python (FastAPI) with server-rendered pages. The site image is DSH plus profile patches; DSH itself is not modified. ## Name The idea of a swarm of cooperating agents was inspired by [openai/swarm](https://github.com/openai/swarm). This is an independent project and is not affiliated with OpenAI. ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © towNingtek inc.

No versioned DSH contract or independently mapped public plugin installation; instructions target the larger Python/Docker host deployment. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # dsh-web-auth [![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@summersec/dsh-web-auth.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@summersec/dsh-web-auth) [![Node.js](https://img.shields.io/badge/node-%3E%3D22-brightgreen)](https://nodejs.org/) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](./LICENSE) [![topic: dsh-plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/topic-dsh--plugin-111827)](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) Transport-level authentication for the [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) (DSH) Web GUI. Official DSH `webserver` serves the GUI, plugin bundles, `/api`, SSE, and WebSocket traffic without a login boundary. This plugin **disables** that unauthenticated carrier and replaces it with a drop-in `webServer` service that authenticates every request **before** it reaches application routes. 中文文档：[README.zh-CN.md](./README.zh-CN.md) --- ## Login page ![DeepSeek Harness authentication page](./docs/assets/dsh-web-auth-login-v0.1.2.png) --- ## Why this exists DSH’s stock web host is convenient for local use, but it is not a product auth layer: - Binding to `0.0.0.0` or putting the port behind a reverse proxy can expose the full control surface. - A frontend-only “login page” does not protect `/api`, static plugin assets, SSE, or WebSocket upgrades. - Session and password handling need to live on the HTTP carrier itself. `@summersec/dsh-web-auth` sits at the transport layer: 1. Disable `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver`. 2. Insert `webserver-auth` with the same `ctx.webServer` contract (`register`, `registerUpgrade`, `registerFallback`, `tapIndex`, `host`, `port`). 3. Gate HTTP and upgrade traffic with a server-side session cookie. Other plugins keep registering routes as usual; they do not need to know auth exists. --- ## Features | Area | Behavior | | --- | --- | | Coverage | HTTP routes **and** WebSocket / HTTP upgrade paths | | Default mode | `always` — login required even on `127.0.0.1` | | Optional mode | `non-loopback` — skip auth only when bound to loopback | | Passwords | scrypt hashes (`scrypt$N$r$p$salt$key`); plaintext env only for temporary use | | Sessions | 32-byte random tokens, in-memory store, sliding TTL | | Cookies | `HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, optional `Secure` | | Abuse control | Per-client-IP login attempt limiter with `Retry-After` | | Login UX | Built-in `/auth/login` page (light/dark), form + JSON body | | Hardening | Origin check on login/logout, open-redirect sanitization, CSP and frame denial on auth responses | --- ## Requirements - **Node.js** `>= 22` - **DeepSeek Harness** with a `web` profile (peer: `@deepseek-ai/cordis` `^4.0.1`) - A password **hash** in the process environment (recommended), or a temporary plaintext password --- ## Quick start ```powershell # 1) Generate a random password + scrypt hash (save the password offline) npx --yes @summersec/dsh-web-auth generate # 2) Export the hash for this shell session (do not commit it) $env:WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH = 'scrypt$...' $env:WEB_AUTH_USERNAME = 'admin' # 3) Install into the web profile dsh plugin --profile web add @summersec/dsh-web-auth # 4) Start the GUI dsh web ``` Open the usual DSH URL. Unauthenticated browser navigations redirect to `/auth/login`. API and other non-HTML clients receive `401` JSON: ```json { "error": "authentication_required" } ``` After login you get a session cookie and continue to the original path. The injected browser bootstrap makes same-origin API, SSE, and plugin requests use that session cookie explicitly. If an in-memory session expires or the service restarts, a JSON `authentication_required` response sends the browser back to the login page instead of leaving the plugin in a silent transport-failure state. > **Do not** put the password or hash into the project `.env` if that file is shared or committed. Prefer the process environment, a secrets manager, or a private host-level env file outside the repo. --- ## Install from source ```powershell git clone https://github.com/SummerSec/dsh-web-auth.git cd dsh-web-auth npm install node .\bin\dsh-web-auth.js generate $env:WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH = 'scrypt$...' # From the parent directory that hosts your DSH workspace, or via local path: dsh plugin --profile web add dsh web ``` Hash an existing password (minimum **12** characters): ```powershell $env:WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD = 'your-long-passphrase' node .\bin\dsh-web-auth.js hash-password Remove-Item Env:WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD ``` Or pipe stdin (the CLI never accepts the password as a command-line argument): ```powershell 'your-long-passphrase' | node .\bin\dsh-web-auth.js hash-password ``` --- ## Authentication modes | `authMode` / `WEB_AUTH_MODE` | When auth runs | | --- | --- | | `always` (**default**) | Always, including `host: 127.0.0.1` | | `non-loopback` | Only when `host` is not `127.0.0.1` (e.g. a concrete LAN IP) | ```powershell # Default: always require login $env:WEB_AUTH_MODE = 'always' dsh web # Loopback without login; binding any non-loopback address gates automatically $env:WEB_AUTH_MODE = 'non-loopback' dsh web --host 192.168.1.20 ``` If authentication is active and neither `passwordHash` nor `password` is configured, the plugin **throws at startup** so you never ship an open server by accident. --- ## Environment variables The bundle (`cordis.patch.yml`) wires these into plugin config: | Variable | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `WEB_AUTH_MODE` | `always` | `always` or `non-loopback` | | `WEB_AUTH_USERNAME` | `admin` | Login username | | `WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH` | _(none)_ | Preferred scrypt hash from `generate` / `hash-password` | | `WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD` | _(none)_ | Plaintext password for temporary / lab use only | Prefer `WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH`. Keep `WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD` for short-lived local experiments. --- ## Advanced configuration The bundle: 1. Sets the stock `webserver` row to `disabled: true`. 2. Inserts `webserver-auth` with name `@summersec/dsh-web-auth`. DSH patches replace config **as a whole**. To override advanced fields, restate the full `webserver-auth` block in the profile patch (e.g. profile `cordis.patch.yml`): ```yaml - id: webserver-auth name: '@summersec/dsh-web-auth' inject: [webStartup] config: host: !!js ctx.webStartup.host ?? '127.0.0.1' port: !!js ctx.webStartup.port ?? 3080 authMode: always username: admin passwordHash: !!js process.env.WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH sessionTtlMinutes: 720 maxAttempts: 5 attemptWindowSeconds: 300 secureCookie: auto trustProxy: false ``` ### Config reference | Field | Type / values | Default | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | `host` | IP or host name | `127.0.0.1` | Listen address; any non-loopback bind forces auth | | `port` | `0`–`65535` | `3080` | Listen port; `0` for ephemeral | | `authMode` | `always` \| `non-loopback` | `always` | See [Authentication modes](#authentication-modes) | | `username` | string | `admin` | Single shared account | | `password` | string | — | Plaintext; avoid in production | | `passwordHash` | `scrypt$...` | — | Required format from the CLI | | `sessionTtlMinutes` | `1`–`43200` | `720` (12h) | Sliding window on each authenticated request | | `maxAttempts` | `1`–`1000` | `5` | Failed logins per IP per window | | `attemptWindowSeconds` | `1`–`86400` | `300` | Attempt window length | | `secureCookie` | `auto` \| `always` \| `never` | `auto` | When to set the `Secure` flag | | `trustProxy` | boolean | `false` | Trust `X-Forwarded-*` only behind a locked-down proxy | ### `secureCookie` and `trustProxy` | Scenario | Suggested settings | | --- | --- | | Local HTTP on loopback | `secureCookie: auto`, `trustProxy: false` | | Direct TLS on the Node process | `secureCookie: auto` (sets `Secure` when the socket is encrypted) | | HTTPS terminated at nginx / Caddy / Cloudflare | `secureCookie: auto` or `always`, **`trustProxy: true`**, and **only** the proxy may reach DSH’s port | If `trustProxy` is true while the port is reachable by untrusted clients, attackers can spoof `X-Forwarded-For` / `X-Forwarded-Proto` and weaken IP limits or cookie security. Lock network access first. --- ## Brute-force protection Failed logins are limited by client IP. With the default configuration, an IP may fail 5 times within 300 seconds. Further attempts receive `429 Too Many Requests` and a `Retry-After` header until the window expires. A successful login clears that IP's failure count. Configure the threshold with: ```yaml maxAttempts: 5 attemptWindowSeconds: 300 ``` The limiter is intentionally small and local: - Counters are stored in process memory, so a restart clears them and multiple instances do not share state. - It limits IP addresses, not accounts. Attackers rotating source IPs can avoid a single-IP threshold. - With `trustProxy: false`, the socket address is used. With `trustProxy: true`, the first `X-Forwarded-For` value is trusted, so the DSH port must only accept traffic from the configured proxy. For an Internet-facing deployment, keep this limiter enabled and add rate limiting at the reverse proxy or firewall. It is not a replacement for HTTPS, network isolation, or a strong password. --- ## Auth HTTP API | Method | Path | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `GET` / `HEAD` | `/auth/login` | Login HTML page; `?next=/path` for post-login redirect | | `POST` | `/auth/login` | Authenticate (`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` or `application/json`) | | `POST` | `/auth/logout` | Clear session cookie and redirect to login | | `GET` | `/auth/status` | `{ authenticated, required, username? }` — `200` or `401` | ### Login body (JSON) ```json { "username": "admin", "password": "...", "next": "/" } ``` ### Behavior notes - Successful form login responds with `303` + `Set-Cookie` (`dsh_web_auth`) and `Location` set to a **sanitized** relative path (blocks `//evil`, absolute URLs, and header-injection characters). - Failed login returns the login page with an error message (`401`) or rate-limit page (`429` + `Retry-After`). - Login and logout require a matching `Origin` when the header is present (CSRF-oriented check). - WebSocket upgrades without a valid session are closed with `401` and a JSON error body. - Auth HTML responses set `Cache-Control: no-store`, a strict CSP, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, and related headers. --- ## How it fits into DSH ```text Browser / client │ ▼ ┌──────────────────────┐ │ dsh-web-auth │ ← session cookie / login routes │ (Authenticated │ │ WebServer service) │ └──────────┬───────────┘ │ authenticated only ▼ GUI · plugin bundles · /api · SSE · WS (registered via ctx.webServer.*) ``` Compatible surface with the stock web server service: - `register({ kind, path, handler })` - `registerUpgrade({ path, handler })` - `registerFallback(handler)` - `tapIndex(transform)` - `host` / `port` getters --- ## CLI Package binary: `dsh-web-auth` ```text dsh-web-auth generate Print WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD=... and WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD_HASH=... dsh-web-auth hash-password Read password from WEB_AUTH_PASSWORD or stdin; print scrypt hash only ``` ### Password hashing algorithm The CLI uses Node.js `crypto.scryptSync`, an RFC 7914 scrypt password-based key derivation function. It is designed to make large-scale password guessing more expensive in both CPU time and memory than a fast general-purpose hash. For each password, the plugin: 1. Generates a new 16-byte random salt with `crypto.randomBytes`. 2. Derives a 64-byte key with `N=16384`, `r=8`, and `p=1`. 3. Stores the algorithm name, parameters, salt, and derived key in one string. The salt and key use unpadded Base64URL encoding. 4. During login, derives the key again with the stored parameters and compares it with `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. The password itself is not stored, and the encoded value is not encryption that can be decrypted. Passwords passed to the hashing CLI must contain at least **12** characters. Stored format: ```text scrypt$N$r$p$$ ``` Default parameters: `N=16384` (CPU/memory cost), `r=8` (block size), `p=1` (parallelization), a 64-byte derived key, and a 16-byte salt. The Node.js scrypt memory ceiling is set to at least 64 MiB for these operations. --- ## Verification ```powershell npm run check # syntax check + unit tests npm pack --dry-run # publish file set dsh --profile web --dump-config ``` In the dump, confirm: - Stock `webserver` has `disabled: true` - A `webserver-auth` row exists with name `@summersec/dsh-web-auth` - Startup logs do not show `FAILED` Manual smoke: 1. Open the GUI without a cookie → redirect to `/auth/login`. 2. Log in → land on the app; cookie `dsh_web_auth` present. 3. `GET /auth/status` with cookie → `authenticated: true`. 4. `POST /auth/logout` → session cleared. 5. Exceed failed attempts → `429` until the window resets. --- ## Publish to npm Package name: `@summersec/dsh-web-auth` (public scope). Publishing is performed only by the repository's GitHub Actions workflow. **Do not use local `npm publish`** as a release path. Before the first release, add a repository Actions secret named `NPM_TOKEN`. It must be an npm token with permission to publish `@summersec` packages, and the npm organization’s 2FA and CI-publishing policy must permit GitHub Actions to use that token. Release through one of these workflow entry points: 1. Create a GitHub Release with a `vX.Y.Z` tag that exactly matches `package.json`'s `X.Y.Z` version. 2. Run **Publish Node.js Package** with `workflow_dispatch` and provide the exact package version. The workflow validates the version, runs checks, then publishes to npm and GitHub Packages. Pushes and pull requests run the verification job only; they cannot publish packages. If GitHub Packages has already published but npm fails, open that workflow run and choose **Re-run failed jobs**. Do not re-run the entire workflow, because that would try to publish the same GitHub Packages version again. --- ## Limitations - **In-memory sessions** — process restart invalidates all logins; no multi-instance sticky session store. - **Single shared account** — one username/password boundary, not multi-user RBAC or audit roles. - **Only the DSH web carrier** — other ports or sidecars need their own protection. - **Not a substitute for TLS** — put HTTPS in front for any non-loopback or multi-user network. - **`trustProxy` is dangerous if mis-scoped** — only enable when the listen port is exclusive to a trusted reverse proxy. --- ## Security notes - Prefer scrypt hashes over plaintext env passwords. - Default `always` mode avoids “I thought loopback was enough” surprises on shared machines. - Cookie flags and Origin checks reduce common session theft and CSRF patterns; they do not replace network isolation and HTTPS. - Report security issues privately if you find one; do not open a public issue with exploit details. --- ## Project layout ```text dsh-web-auth/ ├── bin/dsh-web-auth.js # generate / hash-password CLI ├── cordis.patch.yml # DSH bundle: disable stock webserver, insert webserver-auth ├── src/ │ ├── auth.js # scrypt, sessions, attempt limiter, cookie helpers │ └── index.js # AuthenticatedWebServer service + login UI ├── test/ # node:test unit tests ├── package.json ├── README.md └── README.zh-CN.md ``` --- ## Links - Repository: [github.com/SummerSec/dsh-web-auth](https://github.com/SummerSec/dsh-web-auth) - npm: [@summersec/dsh-web-auth](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@summersec/dsh-web-auth) - Topic: [dsh-plugin](https://github.com/topics/dsh-plugin) - Friends: [LINUX DO](https://linux.do/) --- ## License [MIT](./LICENSE) # Swarm [繁體中文](README.zh-TW.md) | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) | English [![CI](https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/towNingtek/swarm)](https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm/releases) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) An AI office you can host yourself, run by a **swarm**: AI agents take the issues of an EPIC in parallel, a judge accepts their work only when its acceptance criteria pass, and people decide and accept. You run one platform; each customer you invite gets an isolated [DeepSeek Harness (DSH)](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) site that already holds an office template: companies, AI staff roles, schedules and a place for their own keys. ![The operator creates a customer and sends an invite; the customer activates, the site gets built, and they work with the AI in their own site](docs/media/demo.gif) Full video with captions: [docs/media/demo.mp4](docs/media/demo.mp4). The demo runs on a throwaway install with a scripted model, so the AI's replies are canned. > The UI text is currently in Traditional Chinese. ## How the swarm works Swarm turns a goal into **an EPIC of small issues**, hands each issue to an AI agent, and lets the agents work **in parallel**. A result is accepted only when the issue's **executable acceptance criteria** pass, run by a separate judge. People define the goal, release the work and accept the result; they do not need to watch it. Source: [`docs/diagrams/swarm-flow.en.mmd`](docs/diagrams/swarm-flow.en.mmd) | Stage | Who | Gate | |-------|-----|------| | ① Define | Person + `epic` skill | No issue without a testable "done"; every criterion is run first and must fail today; drafts must pass `epic_lint` | | ② Release | Person | Adding `swarm:go` freezes the criteria | | ③ Build and judge | Agents + runner | Each agent works in its own worktree, limited to the files its issue lists; issues on the same file are chained; the runner executes the criteria verbatim and counts only exit codes | | ④ Accept | Person | Review the EPIC pull request (low-risk EPICs may auto-merge); a closing summary feeds the monthly report | ![The board (demo data): planets are open issues on rings by status; clusters are EPICs with their completion arc; red glow means an issue is stuck](docs/media/30-board.png) Every site has the **Wolffia board** at `/board/`: a live view of a GitHub Project where you drag cards to change status, release EPICs, add projects from any org you can see, and ask **📊 Analyse** — the site's own AI reads the board and answers. See [`swarm/`](swarm/) and [`plugins/swarm-board/`](plugins/swarm-board/). ## What it does - **Invite-only sites.** In the admin console you create a customer, pick an office template, set a monthly model quota and send a single-use invite link. The customer picks their own username and password. - **One container per customer.** The platform builds the site by itself: a DSH container with its own login, data and workspace, an nginx route and (optionally) a DNS record. Deleting the customer removes all of it. - **Onboarding page with a setup copilot.** The customer sees setup progress and the site build live. The copilot explains the next step from what the platform actually recorded, and does not make up progress. - **Into the site without a second password.** **Open my site** hands the signed-in customer over with a single-use ticket. - **The platform's model key never enters a site.** Each site gets its own starter key, which only works against the platform's relay. The relay checks that key and the site's monthly budget, then forwards the call with the platform key. - **An office ready on first visit.** The workspace starts with the office template (an `AGENTS.md`, a getting-started guide, a place for companies). Customers can add their own model keys later. - **Conversation sharing.** [dsh-share-room](https://github.com/yillkid/dsh-share-room) is installed in every site, so a customer can invite guests into a conversation. - **Operator view.** One page lists every customer with their site, quota policy and template. When a customer asks for a human, the operator answers from the same console. ## Screenshots | Operator | Customer | |---|---| | ![Operator overview: every site, its usage, last run and what needs attention; 📊 board and site buttons on each card](docs/media/20-admin-overview.png) | ![Customer overview: own site, usage, recent runs, one-click board](docs/media/21-customer-overview.png) | | ![Activating an account from the invite link](docs/media/04-activate.png) | ![Customer settings: setup progress and the site password](docs/media/22-customer-settings.png) | | ![The single-use invite link (masked here)](docs/media/03-admin-invite.png) | ![The onboarding page with the site ready](docs/media/06-site-ready.png) | Inside the customer's own site: the reply comes through the platform relay, and the usage counts toward the monthly quota. ![Working with the AI inside the customer's own site](docs/media/09-site-chat.png) ## How it fits together Source: [`docs/diagrams/architecture.en.mmd`](docs/diagrams/architecture.en.mmd) Each site sits on an isolated Docker network. The relay is the only host port it can reach: no other host ports, private networks or cloud metadata. The platform never runs `sudo`. Two small root units do the privileged work, one for the firewall and one that applies nginx configs. Details: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) and [docs/security.md](docs/security.md). ## Before you run it - **Use a host dedicated to Swarm.** The platform user is in the `docker` group, which is equivalent to root. - **Containers are not VMs.** All customers share one kernel and one Docker daemon. DSH's in-site sandbox does not work in a container, so the container, network and firewall are the only containment. - **Sites can reach the internet.** A customer's AI can send that customer's data anywhere. - **You pay for the starter model.** Every site's starter calls go through your gateway on your key. Monthly caps are enforced, but token counts are estimates. - **TLS is yours.** Nothing here terminates TLS. Put certbot, a load balancer or a tunnel in front. The full list is under [Known limits](docs/security.md#known-limits). ## Install You need a Linux host (Ubuntu 22.04 or similar) with Docker 24+, nginx and Python 3.10+, about 2 GB of disk for the site image, and an OpenAI-compatible model gateway (for example LiteLLM). Point `platform.` and `*.` at the host. ```sh sudo git clone https://github.com/towNingtek/swarm /opt/swarm cd /opt/swarm sudo python3 -m venv .venv && sudo .venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt sudo docker build -f site/Dockerfile -t swarm-site:latest . sudo deploy/install.sh sudo editor /etc/swarm/platform.env # domain, origins, model gateway sudo editor /etc/swarm/secrets/model-key sudo cp deploy/nginx/swarm-platform.conf.example /etc/nginx/conf.d/swarm-platform.conf sudo editor /etc/nginx/conf.d/swarm-platform.conf && sudo nginx -t && sudo systemctl reload nginx sudo deploy/install.sh --start ``` Then open `https://platform./admin` and sign in with the password in `/etc/swarm/secrets/admin-password`. The rest of the settings, logs and the first customer are covered in [deploy/README.md](deploy/README.md). The whole install is tested from scratch in a throwaway container: `bash deploy/tests/clean-install/run.sh`. ## Repository | Path | What it is | |---|---| | [`platform/`](platform/) | The platform, the admin console and the site model relay | | [`site/`](site/) | The site engine and the DSH site image | | [`office-template/`](office-template/) | The office every new site starts with | | [`plugins/`](plugins/) | DSH plugins kept here: branding, and the board (Wolffia) with the `epic` skill | | [`swarm/`](swarm/) | The swarm orchestrator: agents, the judge, autostart, summaries and reports | | [`deploy/`](deploy/) | Install on one host with systemd, Docker and nginx | | [`demo/`](demo/) | The scripted model and recording scripts behind the demo above | | [`docs/`](docs/) | Architecture, security model, HTTP API, design records, swarm contracts | ## Development ```sh bash scripts/test.sh # every suite; Python 3.10+, Node 22 ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for how issues are written here (EPICs with executable acceptance criteria) and what a pull request needs. The platform is Python (FastAPI) with server-rendered pages. The site image is DSH plus profile patches; DSH itself is not modified. ## Name The idea of a swarm of cooperating agents was inspired by [openai/swarm](https://github.com/openai/swarm). This is an independent project and is not affiliated with OpenAI. ## Security Please report vulnerabilities privately. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License [MIT](LICENSE) © towNingtek inc.

# dsh-cost-tracker

DeepSeek Harness（DSH）多平台费用追踪插件：**按模型自动切换计费口径**，每轮对话结算花费，
三个平台余额统一呈现，并给 WorkBuddy 模型加档位与促销标签。

## 成本观：为什么不是按单价排序

三个平台花的**不是同一种钱**：

| 优先级 | 平台 | 花的是什么钱 | 适用场景 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 第 1 | WorkBuddy 免费模型 | **不花钱** | `hy3`、`step-5-preview`，长短任务都能用 |
| 第 2 | 阿里云百炼 | **虚拟钱**（抵用券） | **长任务 / 大上下文优先**，100 万上下文 |
| 第 3 | WorkBuddy 付费模型 | **免费积分**（每日可再生） | 短对话 |
| 第 4 | DeepSeek 官方 | **真钱** | 最后才用，花一分少一分 |

**优先级按「花不花真钱 / 资源可不可再生」排序，不是按单价。**

积分每日免费补充、可再生；抵用券用完就没；真钱花一分少一分。

### 一个必须记住的实测结论

WorkBuddy 长任务 token 消耗极大（实测单轮 311 万 / 607 万 token）。
付费模型倍率一乘，积分掉得极快。所以：

- **长任务 → 阿里云**（抵用券够用；或 `step-5-preview`，免费且 100 万上下文）
- **短对话 → WorkBuddy 付费模型**（花积分，不心疼）

### 三个平台的时段规则不同

| 平台 | 规则 | 实际效果 |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek 官方 | 工作日 9-12、14-18 高峰；周末与法定节假日全天谷价 | 全天 20 小时是谷价，仅工作日 4 小时高峰 |
| 阿里云百炼 | 东八区 22:00-次日 8:00 闲时，其余忙时 | 白天 14 小时（8-22）全是忙时 |
| WorkBuddy | 积分制，**每个模型自己声明促销时段与折扣** | 不能用统一规则套 |

> ⚠️ **重要**：WorkBuddy 的折扣是「按模型 + 时间窗」声明的
> （源码里是 `discount.schedule` / `discount.factor`），**不能套用 DeepSeek 官方峰谷**。
> 比如「非高峰 5 折」只对 `deepseek-v4.1-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro` 成立，
> `space-bunny` 没有这个规则。本插件只显示上游给出的 `credits` 与 `badges`，不跨模型套规则。

#### 价目表（元 / 百万 token，数组为 `[闲时, 忙时]`）

| 平台 | 缓存命中 hit | 未命中输入 miss | 输出 out |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek 官方 | 0.02 / 0.04 | 1 / 2 | 4 / 8 |
| 阿里云百炼 | 0.1 / 0.2 | 1 / 2 | 4 / 8 |

两者唯一差异是**缓存命中价贵 5 倍**；miss 与 out 相同。

## 功能

### 1. 多平台统一记账

监听会话事件，按 turn 聚合 token，一轮结束时结算：

```
金额 = cacheRead/1e6 × hit价 + input/1e6 × miss价 + output/1e6 × out价
```

`reasoningTokens` 已含在 `outputTokens` 内，不重复累加。

#### 结算触发：为什么不用 `turn/end`

DSH 0.2.1-rc.2 的事件目录里**没有 `turn/end`**。本插件用双保险：

1. **主路径**：`session/event` 里按 `event.type` 分派（含 turn + end/stop/finish 字样即结算）
2. **兜底**：`agent/turn-stopping`（语义是「本轮即将收尾，模型不会再回复」）

结算函数幂等：同一 session 的桶取不到就跳过，两条路径都触发也只记一次账。

`turnAggs` 用 `Map` 按 `sessionId` 分桶，避免多会话并发串账。

### 2. 按模型自动切换计费口径

按 provider 判定平台：

1. `provider` 或 `model` 含 `workbuddy` → WorkBuddy（积分制，不做 token 计价）
2. `provider` ∈ {`deepseek-account`, `deepseek`, `deepseek-official`} → DeepSeek 官方
3. `ctx.get('llm').listProviders()` 查 `baseURL` 含 `aliyuncs` → 阿里云
4. 模型名含 `deepseek` 兜底 → 阿里云

### 3. WorkBuddy 余额采样与账号健康

每轮结束后采样积分余额，与上次相减得本轮消耗。

**两种失效情况不报数：**

| 情况 | 处理 |
|---|---|
| 基准过旧（默认超过 30 分钟未采样） | 不报数——否则会把中间时段消耗都算进来 |
| 余额上升（充值或发放新权益） | 不报数，仅更新基准 |

**健康检查三种状态：**

| 状态 | 级别 |
|---|---|
| 未登录 | error |
| 令牌已过期 | error |
| 令牌 3 天内到期 | warn |

`refresh()` 只更新快照、**不推进基准**——避免「看一眼健康状态」就吃掉上一轮的结算基准。

### 4. 模型列表标签（前端半身）

#### 先说限制：无法跨 provider 交错排序

DSH 模型选择器**先按 provider 分组，组内保留第三方 catalog 顺序**
（`dsh-client-ui-model-selection` 文档原文：
"Both entries group models by provider, third-party providers retain their catalog order."）。

所以做不到「WorkBuddy 免费 → 阿里云 → WorkBuddy flash」的全局顺序。
本插件只能在 WorkBuddy 组内做标签与排序。

#### 标签显示

模型列表里每个 WorkBuddy 模型显示 **模型名 + 若干标签**：

```
Hy4 preview         [常 用] [夜 间 免 费]
Hy3                 [免 费] [额 度 限 制]
Step-5-Preview      [免 费]
Deepseek-V4.1-Flash [主 力] [夜 间 折 扣]
GLM-5.2             [常 用] [夜 间 折 扣]
Kimi-K3-1           [少 用]
```

**档位**（四档，高饱和实心块）：

| 档位 | 颜色 | 含义 |
|---|---|---|
| 免费 | 深绿 `#15803d` | `free === true` |
| 主力 | 深蓝 `#1d4ed8` | `deepseek-v4.1-flash` |
| 常用 | 深橙 `#b45309` | `glm-5.3-flash`、`space-bunny`、`minimax-m2.7`、`hy4-preview` |
| 少用 | 深灰 `#4b5563` | 其余 |

**促销标签**：来自上游 `badges`（实时，不硬编码免费时间表）

**夜间折扣**：`deepseek-v4.1-flash` / `deepseek-v4-pro` 上游不给 badge，
按官方峰谷规则本地推算，每分钟重算——非高峰显示 `夜 间 折 扣`，高峰显示 `高 峰 原 价`

**额度限制**：`hy3`（每日赠额，用尽后转付费）

**限流标记**：被限流/额度用尽的模型直接显示红底「限 流」标签，
不用悬停也能一眼看出不能用；悬停显示精确恢复时间 + 每秒跳动的倒计时。

#### 悬停说明

鼠标悬停模型项，在**模型列表右侧外层**显示两行：

```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ 0.29x 倍率                        │
│ 9月11日–10月31日，每晚 23:00—      │
│ 次日 8:00 享免费额度。             │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

位置固定在列表右边界外，**不跟随鼠标、不遮挡列表**。
深色底（`#1f2937`）+ 白字，18/20px，与浅色列表强对比。

#### 只在模型选择列表生效

内核 `renderModelLabel` 有三个 `placement` 取值，本插件严格区分：

| placement | 位置 | 本插件行为 |
|---|---|---|
| `trigger` | 主界面输入框的当前模型名 | **原样返回，完全不改动** |
| `menu` | 折叠层的当前模型名 | **原样返回** |
| `option` | 下拉列表里的模型项 | 加标签 + 悬停说明 |

代码里就一行守卫：`if (placement !== 'option') return rawName`

#### 两条硬性约束（踩过的坑）

**1. 返回空字符串会吞掉模型名。**
内核是 `renderSlot(slot, props, { fallback: model.name })`——
只有返回 `null`/`undefined` 才用 fallback。返回 `''` 会被当成有效内容，模型名就没了。
本组件所有分支都保证返回非空。

**2. 不能吞掉模型项的鼠标事件。**
选择动作依赖 click 冒泡，标签一律 `pointerEvents: none`。

**3. 浮层必须 portal 到 body。**
模型列表容器是 `position: fixed; overflow: hidden`，
插在列表项内部的内容会被裁掉或顶开下面的模型项。

### 5. 阿里云抵用券：为什么不做 token 计价

实测阿里云官方代金券流水（552 笔 + 189 笔）发现：

- 单笔金额跨 **6 个数量级**（`-0.0002025472` 到 `-25`）
- 余额链条有 **84 处并发断链**（同一秒多笔写入互相覆盖）
- 同一秒多笔、间隔仅数秒——是**流式请求的分段计费**

**决定性对比**（2026-10-19 19:43 那轮，`provider=fufu`）：

| 项 | 数值 |
|---|---|
| token 用量 | in=203, cache=470,272, out=475 |
| token × 忙时单价（手算） | **0.09826 元** |
| 阿里云实际扣减（CSV） | **2.611903 元** |
| 偏差 | **26.6 倍** |

阿里云按「请求级 / 分段级」出账，且含联网搜索等附加功能费，
**token 单价完全推不出真实扣减**。

**所以阿里云只累计 token 用量作参考，余额完全依赖 CSV 校准。**

#### 如何校准

从阿里云控制台「费用与成本 → 明细账单」导出代金券流水 CSV，然后：

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/cost-tracker/aliyun/calibrate \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"path": "C:\\path\\to\\xxx_coupon_use_flow.csv"}'
```

或用 `{"csv": "<CSV 原文>"}` 直接传内容。

返回的 `spentSincePreviousCalibration` 即两次校准之间的真实消耗，可用来核对账目。

### 6. DeepSeek 官方余额（真钱）

经 `deepseekAccount.getBalance()` 读取，**实时真实**。

```json
{
  "available": 40.00,
  "recharged": 20.00,
  "bonus": 20.00,
  "currency": "CNY",
  "error": null
}
```

**必须把充值钱包与赠金钱包一起看** —— 只看 `value`（充值）会漏掉 `bonusWallets`（赠金），
只登录客户端的账号常常只有赠金。本插件对齐 DSH 账号卡片的判据，两边一起求和。

> ⚠️ **实现要点**：`ctx.get('deepseekAccount')` 只能取到**当前注入作用域内可见**的服务。
> 放在 `apply(ctx)` 顶层调用会返回 `undefined`。必须单独开
> `ctx.inject(['deepseekAccount'], cb)` 作用域，在该作用域内取。
> 但**绝不能把 `deepseekAccount` 写进 `inject` 数组**——老宿主没这个服务时，
> 整个插件会永远等不到服务而完全不 apply。

### 7. 费用挂件（widget.js，自动注入页面）

固定 230px 宽的深色小卡片，通过 `webserver/index-inject` 的**内联 script 行**
注入到 DSH 页面（不能用 script-src：加载失败会 reject `__DSH_BOOT_READY__`
让整个应用起不来——dsh-whale-widget issue #154 的教训）。

```
┌────────────────────────────┐
│ 💰 费用                  ▾ │
├────────────────────────────┤
│ ● DeepSeek    ¥40.37       │  真钱
│ ● 阿里云券    ¥XXX.XX      │  抵用券
│ ● WorkBuddy   XXXX 积分    │
│ ────────────────────────── │
│ 单轮 #96       免费        │
│ 今天 8 轮   ¥0.10 / 3 积分 │
│ 本月 60 轮  ¥3.07 / 43 积分│
│ ────────────────────────── │
│ 💡 当前 xxx 消耗积分，      │
│    yyy 现在免费，切过去更省 │
│ ────────────────────────── │
│ 非高峰时段                  │
│ 1. GLM-5.3-Flash           │
│ 2. Space-Bunny             │
└────────────────────────────┘
```

- **记账双档**：单轮费用 + 当天/当月（北京时区自然日/月），阿里云不参与
- **主动建议**：红（当前模型不可用）/ 黄（有更省的）/ 绿（已最优）
- 可折叠、可拖动、位置记 localStorage；四边按卡片实际尺寸钳制，不会拖出界面
- 数据 60 秒自动刷新

### 8. 分时段省钱推荐（lib/recommend.js）

回答两个问题：**现在用哪个最省？首选不能用了换谁？**

- 按当前时段计算每个模型的**实际倍率**（含夜间免费/夜间折扣/官方峰谷 5 折）
- 排序：可用免费 > 实际倍率 > 思考成本（同倍率下默认思考低的优先）> 常用度
- **实时排除**：限流中的模型直接淘汰；免费额度用尽的按付费替代倍率（x0.05）参与排序
- 上下文过滤：长文场景（≥90 万）自动淘汰装不下的模型
- 峰谷判定复用 pricing.js（含周末 + 法定节假日全天谷价），本模块不自己实现
- 时段标签四类：工作日高峰 / 工作日非高峰 / 周末 / 法定节假日

**限额状态必须持久化**（`state.limits`）：内存标记一重启就丢，
用户标记的「额度用尽」会失效——实测教训。变更即写盘，启动即恢复。

**手动标记接口**（上游 status 不返回限额数据时的兜底）：

```bash
curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:<port>/cost-tracker/model-state \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"hy3","state":"exhausted","hours":12}'
```

## 配置（通用化）

插件开箱即用（内置一份默认模型清单），但**每个人的模型、倍率、常用度都不同**。
在你的 `cordis.patch.yml` 的 cost-tracker 行下加 `config:` 覆盖：

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: cost-tracker
      name: dsh-cost-tracker
      config:
        # 遵循「工作日 9-12/14-18 高峰原价、其余谷价」的模型
        peakModels: [deepseek-v4.1-flash, deepseek-v4-pro]
        # 每日赠额型模型（额度用尽转 429/付费）
        quotaModels: [hy3]
        # 推荐排序的同分优先项
        preferred: [deepseek-v4.1-flash, glm-5.3-flash]
        # 标签档位
        tiers:
          main: [deepseek-v4.1-flash]
          common: [glm-5.3-flash, space-bunny]
        # 促销时间窗说明（可选；不配则悬停显示上游 badge 原文）
        promoDesc:
          hy4-preview: 每晚 23:00—次日 8:00 享免费额度（以官方公告为准）。
```

不配置也能跑：内置清单作为开箱示例；但推荐排序与档位标签
只对示例清单准确，**按自己的实际情况覆盖才有意义**。
## HTTP 路由

| 路由 | 方法 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| `/cost-tracker/summary` | GET | 汇总（各平台花费、三个余额、健康、最近 20 轮） |
| `/cost-tracker/ledger` | GET | 记账：单轮费用 + 当天/当月双档（仿小鲸鱼；阿里云不参与） |
| `/cost-tracker/session` | GET | 本次会话花费（按 session 聚合） |
| `/cost-tracker/turn` | GET | 最近一轮 |
| `/cost-tracker/turns` | GET | 每轮消耗明细（`?limit=50&platform=workbuddy`） |
| `/cost-tracker/health` | GET | WorkBuddy 账号健康（顺带采样） |
| `/cost-tracker/aliyun` | GET | 阿里云抵用券余额视图 |
| `/cost-tracker/aliyun/calibrate` | POST | 用官方 CSV 校准抵用券余额 |
| `/cost-tracker/deepseek-balance` | GET | 官方余额；`?force=1` 跳过 60 秒缓存 |
| `/cost-tracker/recommend` | GET | 分时段省钱推荐（实时排除限流/额度用尽的模型） |
| `/cost-tracker/model-limits` | GET | 模型倍率、上下文、思考强度、限流状态 |
| `/cost-tracker/models` | GET | WorkBuddy 模型排序 + 徽章表 |
| `/cost-tracker/model-state` | POST | 手动标记额度用尽/清除（上游不提供限额数据时的兜底） |
| `/cost-tracker/reset` | GET | 清空统计（保留阿里云校准基准） |
| `/cost-tracker/widget.js` | GET | 页面挂件脚本（由插件自动注入，无需手动访问） |

端口每次启动可能变，用 `ctx.webServer.getOrigin()` 取，或看 Web GUI 地址栏。

### 三个平台的余额来源

| 平台 | 字段 | 性质 |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek 官方（真钱） | `deepseekBalance.available` | 实时真实 |
| 阿里云抵用券（虚拟钱） | `aliyun.calibratedBalance` | CSV 校准 |
| WorkBuddy（积分） | `workbuddy.credits` | 实时真实 |

## 限流与上下文溢出

监听 `agent/request-error`，识别两类上游错误：

| 错误 | 识别 | 展示 |
|---|---|---|
| `400 client`「内容过长」 | 正则匹配 | 详情里标「上次因内容过长失败」 |
| `429 soft_rate` | 正则 + 解析报文里的重置时间 | 显示「免费恢复：X 小时 Y 分」倒计时 |

`hy3` 额度用尽后 WorkBuddy 会转到 `hy3-x` 按 x0.05 计费
（DSH 侧不会自动切换，客户端才有这个行为）。

## 安装

```bash
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:<本插件目录的绝对路径>
```

装完重启客户端。

## 数据与隐私

| 项 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 状态文件 | 只写 `$DSH_HOME/.cost-tracker.json` |
| 代码内容 | 无用户名路径、无账号 uid/uin、无 token、无 API Key |
| 账号标识 | 输出前脱敏，只保留前 8 位 |
| WorkBuddy status | 走本机回环，只校验 Host/Origin 为回环，不需要会话凭据 |
| CSV 解析 | 只输出统计量，不保留账号名 |

## 健壮性

- 所有外部调用（读状态、请求路由、调 llm / deepseekAccount 服务）都包 try/catch
- `turnAggs` 用 `Map` 按 `sessionId` 分桶
- 结算函数幂等，多条触发路径不会重复记账
- 节假日表未覆盖当前年份时，峰谷判定退化为「全谷价」并打日志——宁少算不多算

## 已知限制

| 限制 | 说明 |
|---|---|
| 跨 provider 排序 | DSH 按 provider 分组，无法交错 |
| 模型描述 / 免费时段 | `dsh-workbuddy-connect` 的 status 接口不返回这两项；国内版不解析 `modelPromotions`，所以截图里 WorkBuddy 客户端的促销时间窗文字在 DSH 侧拿不到 |
| 阿里云余额精度 | token 估算与真实扣减有偏差（26.6 倍），只用 CSV 校准 |
| `turn/end` 不存在 | 用 `session/event` 分派 + `agent/turn-stopping` 兜底 |
| `workspace.toast` 不可用 | key 域已满，冒泡提醒需改用 `shell.overlay` |
| hy3 自动转付费 | `dsh-workbuddy-connect` 没实现，429 直接报错；上游参数名未知，未擅自猜测 |

permissions.network: the configured relay (default: the shared server above), STUN servers, and UDP to the peer machines. The optional chatops channels reach one instant-messaging platform each, and only when that channel is named in `channels` and the host has supplied the transport: the WeChat channel reaches ilinkai.weixin.qq.com and sends the bot token as a bearer credential, and both that host and the base url in a login response are checked against an allow-list before a token is sent anywhere
permissions.filesystem: read/write inside the project directory and DSH_HOME; the agent writes its spool and state under --state; the chatops file fence reads inside `projectRoot` only, after resolving symlinks

manifest.name: @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin
manifest.description: Run one project across your own Windows and macOS machines from a single DeepSeek account, through 11 w2m_* tools. Four coordination modes (replicate, split, broadcast, pipeline) and six aggregate verdicts (consistent, divergent, divergent-platform, failed, partial, unverifiable). P2P hole punching by default, with a bundled relay, STUN responder and ledger fallback, so the fleet needs no third-party service. Joining needs a pairing code plus autoStartAgent: true; installing alone does not join.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# DSH: Windows2MacOS

**One DeepSeek account. One instruction. Every machine you own runs the same project.**

[![CI](https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin?label=npm)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin)
[![DSH plugin](https://img.shields.io/badge/DSH-plugin-4c6ef5)](#1-dsh-plugin-recommended--zero-configuration)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE)
[![platforms](https://img.shields.io/badge/CI-windows%20%7C%20macos%20%7C%20linux-4c6ef5)](#verified-and-not-verified)

English | [中文](#中文说明)

---

## Install

Five routes in. They all end with **15 tools registered** in your agent. Pick one.

### 1. DSH plugin (recommended — zero configuration)

```bash
# 1. install the package into your DSH profile
dsh plugin add @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin

# 2. name it in the profile's bundle list — a package that is not bundled never loads
#    ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/dsh.profile.yml
plugins:
  - '@twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin'

# 3. restart DSH; joining happens at mount time, so a hot reload is not enough
```

Since **1.1.15** the agent starts by itself (`autoStartAgent` defaults to `true`): a freshly installed machine
derives its account identity, joins the account's fleet, and shows up in `w2m_devices` with no pairing step.
To turn that off, patch the **existing** `w2m` row — do not add a second one:

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml
- id: w2m
  config:
    autoStartAgent: false
```

### 2. npm (MCP server, any client)

```bash
npm install -g @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin
w2m-mcp --help
```

Point any MCP client at `w2m-mcp`. **Zero runtime dependencies**; the package ships the relay, the agent and the
tools.

### 3. Claude Code

```bash
/plugin marketplace add TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos
/plugin install w2m@twinsearth
```

The manifests live in [`.claude-plugin/`](.claude-plugin/) and are version-locked to the release.

### 4. Codex and other MCP-capable CLIs

```toml
# copy this block into your own codex/mcp-servers.toml
[mcp_servers.w2m]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin@1.1.19", "w2m-mcp"]
```

### 5. Verified release tarball (offline)

From the `v1.1.19` release page download **both** files — `twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-1.1.19.tgz` and `SHA256SUMS` —
then:

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/releases/download/v1.1.19/twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-1.1.19.tgz
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS          # verify before installing, always
npm install -g ./twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-1.1.19.tgz
```

Every release carries `SHA256SUMS` for exactly this reason. If a release is missing it, do not install that release.

### 6. Beta (prerelease — never on npm)

A beta is a **GitHub prerelease**, not an npm version. Nothing about it is resolved by `npm install`, and `latest` never
points at one. It exists for a developer who has been granted `beta-access` and accepts that it can break.

```bash
# 1. find the newest prerelease (a beta is marked "Pre-release" on the releases page)
#    https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/releases  -> latest entry labelled Pre-release
# 2. download BOTH files attached to it: twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-<version>.tgz and SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS          # verify before installing, always
npm install -g ./twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-<version>.tgz
```

- **Access**: the beta workflow waits on the protected `beta-access` environment, so a reviewer must approve each run
  before the artifact exists at all.
- **Risk acknowledgment**: install it only if you have read [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and accept that a beta may fail
  where a stable release does not.
- **Going back**: `npm install -g @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin@latest` returns you to the stable channel.
- **Why not npm**: there is no `npm publish` line in the beta workflow. A channel cannot leak into the default install if
  the publication cannot happen at all.


---

## Quick start

```text
w2m_status                       # am I paired? which fleet?
w2m_devices                      # what is in the fleet?
w2m_run mode="replicate" command_argv=["git","rev-parse","HEAD"]
w2m_wait task_id="..."
```

`replicate` runs on every online machine; the verdict is `consistent` only when every machine returned the same
result **and** the same commit anchor. `split` gives each machine a slice, `pipeline` chains stages, `broadcast`
names one executor and reports observers, `compose` merges results.

---

## What it is

An installable plugin that turns a set of machines into **one fleet**, keyed by **your account**, not by a
hand-maintained host list.

| Piece | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| **Relay** | a small HTTP server: task routing, leases, SSE, blob storage. Run it anywhere your machines can reach. |
| **Agent** | runs on each machine: pairs once, executes allow-listed commands, heartbeats. |
| **Plugin** | the tools your agent calls. |
| **Admission** (1.1.14+) | a new machine asks to join; an online member approves, **10 s auto-approves**, and a machine admitted in the last 24 h can be removed immediately. |

### Tools

`w2m_status` · `w2m_devices` · `w2m_run` · `w2m_wait` · `w2m_history` · `w2m_stats` · `w2m_report` ·
`w2m_memory` · `w2m_approvals` · `w2m_cancel` · `w2m_council` · `w2m_chat` · `w2m_update` `w2m_tasks`
- `w2m_intent` — map a structured intent (run-tests, node-version, git-status, git-head, fleet-facts, shard-probe) onto an allow-listed command; unknown intents are refused by name, never guessed.

### Environment a dispatched command receives (1.1.15+)

Values come from the offer, never from argv, so one machine cannot reshape a fleet-wide split.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `W2M_INDEX` / `W2M_INDEX_TOTAL` | this machine's slice number and how many slices exist |
| `W2M_STAGE_INDEX` | the pipeline stage; deliberately separate from `W2M_INDEX` |
| `W2M_TASK_ID` / `W2M_MODE` | the task and its mode |
| `W2M_MACHINE_ID` / `W2M_MACHINE_NAME` | this machine |

So `command_argv=["node","-e","process.exit(Number(process.env.W2M_INDEX)+1)"]` over four machines exits 1/2/3/4.
Single-machine behaviour is tested; the four-machine run is listed as **not verified** below.

---

## Fleet model

Identity is **the account**, not a list of hosts. A machine derives an Ed25519 identity from its account
material; the relay registers the matching public key when the account's first machine pairs; every later machine
proves the same account with a one-time signed challenge.

If the old pairing path fails for a **named** reason only — invalid pairing code, unreachable relay, timeout — the
machine falls back to asking for admission. Any other failure needs a human and does **not** change mechanisms. A
rejection is final; the machine does not re-ask.

The relay is authoritative for every time window and every quorum, because client clocks disagree (measured:
tens of seconds between machines in one fleet):

- **10 s** without a decision auto-approves, but only while at least one member is **online** — an empty fleet
  cannot consent, and that refusal is named (`NO_ONLINE_MEMBER`);
- within **24 h** of admission, any online member may remove the machine immediately;
- after 24 h a single machine may only **open a vote**, whose quorum set is **frozen at open time** so a voter
  going offline mid-vote cannot move the bar;
- the quorum is 3+ old members need **≥ 50 %** (rounded up); a two-member fleet needs **one** vote;
- a machine offline for more than **72 hours** leaves the **list** — it is never deleted, its records stay, and it
  returns by reporting again.

---

## Security posture

- The command allow-list is **argv-prefix** based and rejects argv-reparsing flags (`--import`, appended `-e`) with
  `COMMAND_REPARSE_ARGUMENT`. It is a boundary, not a sandbox.
- Dispatching tasks requires an operator token. A device token cannot dispatch.
- Admission approval requires at least one member online.
- The account signing key is derived from the fleet key, **never** from the account code — the account code is
  written to logs, and deriving a key from a readable value would hand out the account identity.
- Every release is checksummed.

---

## Verified and not verified

A green badge that hides this is worse than no badge.

**Verified:** 2458 tests in 102 files (2444 pass, 14 skip), 15 pre-flight checks, CI green on Windows, macOS and
Linux, npm + GitHub release + checksums consistent, end-to-end fleet runs on a real Linux/Mac/Windows triple.

**Not verified / known gaps:**

| Gap | State |
|---|---|
| Approval **popup** control | the relay enforces the rules and `w2m_approvals` · `w2m_cancel` lists and settles requests, but the 10 s countdown is relay data shown in a list, not a dedicated popup |
| Four-machine `W2M_INDEX` run | single-machine behaviour tested; the fleet-wide 1/2/3/4 run has not been executed |
| Fleet chat / broadcast channel | message store + quota implemented and tested; encryption, sharding, endpoints and the panel are **not built** |
| P2P on some macOS hosts | `P2P_PUNCH_FAILED: Unknown cipher` observed; the task falls back to the relay path |

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| installed, but `w2m_devices` answers 401 | the agent never started, so no device token | check `autoStartAgent` is not `false`; restart DSH (not a hot reload) |
| machine missing from the fleet | the plugin is not in `dsh.profile.bundles` | add it — a package that is not bundled never loads |
| `COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED` | command not in the allow-list | extend the allow-list; argv is matched by prefix |
| verdict always `partial` | a stale lease from a machine that is down | fixed in 1.1.2: a dispatch leases only online, non-silent machines |
| `P2P_PUNCH_FAILED` | NAT, or a host crypto gap | it downgrades to the relay path; results are unaffected |

---

## Release channels

Three channels, and only one of them is what \
pm install\ gives you.

| Channel | Where it comes from | Who should use it |
|---|---|---|
| **stable** | npm \latest\ — a version the developer declared stable | everyone; this is the default install |
| **beta** | a GitHub **prerelease** (tarball + \SHA256SUMS\), **never on npm** | developers granted \ eta-access\ who accept that it can fail |
| **latest build** | the newest of the two, whatever its channel | a developer who wants the newest code and knows the above |

A bump is a **beta by default**. npm receives a version only when the developer says, in so many words, that this one is a
stable release: a beta is published as a prerelease (so neither GitHub nor npm ever resolves it as \latest\), it is
downloadable only after the \ eta-access\ environment approves the run, and installing it requires reading
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) and accepting the risk.

There is no \
pm publish\ line in the beta workflow. That is deliberate — a channel cannot leak to the default install if
the publication cannot happen at all.
---

- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) — every version, including what it deliberately did **not** ship
- [PLATFORMS](docs/PLATFORMS.md) — Claude Code, Codex and MCP wiring details
- [Releases](https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/releases) — per-release evidence and checksums
- [Issues](https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/issues)

## 中文说明

**一个 DeepSeek 账号。一句话。你自己的每一台机器跑同一个项目。**

以下内容与上方英文**逐节对应**，不是摘要。

### 安装

五种方式，最终都会在你的 agent 里注册 **15 tools registered**。任选其一。

#### 1. DSH 插件（推荐，零配置）

```bash
# 1. 把包装进你的 DSH profile
dsh plugin add @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin

# 2. 在 profile 的 bundle 列表里写上包名 —— 没进 bundle 的包永远不会被加载
#    ~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/dsh.profile.yml
plugins:
  - '@twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin'

# 3. 重启 DSH。加入编队发生在 mount 时，热重载不够
```

从 **1.1.15** 起 agent 会自动启动（`autoStartAgent` 默认 `true`）：新装的机器自行派生账号身份、加入该账号的
编队，无需配对步骤就会出现在 `w2m_devices` 里。若要关闭，请 patch **已存在的** `w2m` 行，**不要新增第二行**：

```yaml
# cordis.patch.yml
- id: w2m
  config:
    autoStartAgent: false
```

#### 2. npm（MCP 服务器，任意客户端）

```bash
npm install -g @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin
w2m-mcp --help
```

把任意 MCP 客户端指向 `w2m-mcp`。**零运行时依赖**；包里同时带有 relay、agent 与工具。

#### 3. Claude Code

```bash
/plugin marketplace add TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos
/plugin install w2m@twinsearth
```

清单文件位于 [`.claude-plugin/`](.claude-plugin/)，版本与发行版锁定。

#### 4. Codex 及其它支持 MCP 的 CLI

```toml
# 把这段复制进你自己的 codex/mcp-servers.toml
[mcp_servers.w2m]
command = "npx"
args = ["-y", "@twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin@1.1.19", "w2m-mcp"]
```

#### 5. 校验过的发布包（离线）

从 `v1.1.19` 的 release 页面下载**两个**文件 —— `twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-1.1.19.tgz` 与 `SHA256SUMS` —— 然后：

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/releases/download/v1.1.19/twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-1.1.19.tgz
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS          # 安装前务必校验
npm install -g ./twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-1.1.19.tgz
```

每个 release 都带 `SHA256SUMS` 正是为了这一步。若某个 release 缺少它，**不要安装该版本**。

#### 6. Beta（预发布版 —— 不进 npm）

Beta 是 **GitHub prerelease**，不是 npm 版本：`npm install` 永远拿不到它，`latest` 也不会指向它。它是给**已获
`beta-access` 授权、且接受它可能出问题**的开发者用的。

```bash
# 1. 在 releases 页面找标着 Pre-release 的最新条目
#    https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/releases
# 2. 下载该条目的两个文件：twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-<版本>.tgz 与 SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS          # 安装前务必校验
npm install -g ./twinsearth-w2m-dsh-plugin-<版本>.tgz
```

- **权限**：beta 流水线挂在受保护的 `beta-access` 环境上，**每次运行都需要审批者批准**，产物才会存在；
- **风险确认**：安装前请阅读 [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)，并接受 beta 可能比稳定版更容易失败；
- **回退**：`npm install -g @twinsearth/w2m-dsh-plugin@latest` 即回到稳定版通道；
- **为什么不走 npm**：beta 工作流里**没有 `npm publish`** —— 只要发布动作不可能发生，这个通道就漏不进默认安装。


### 快速开始

```text
w2m_status                       # 我配对了吗？在哪个编队？
w2m_devices                      # 编队里有什么？
w2m_run mode="replicate" command_argv=["git","rev-parse","HEAD"]
w2m_wait task_id="..."
```

`replicate` 在每一台在线机器上执行；只有当所有机器返回**相同结果**且**相同 commit 锚点**时，裁决才是
`consistent`。`split` 给每台机器一个分片，`pipeline` 串联多个阶段，`broadcast` 指定一个执行者并汇报观察者，
`compose` 合并结果。

### 它是什么

一个可安装插件，把一组机器变成**一个编队**，以**你的账号**为键，而不是靠手工维护的主机清单。

| 组件 | 职责 |
|---|---|
| **Relay** | 一个小型 HTTP 服务：任务路由、租约、SSE、blob 存储。放在任何机器可达的位置。 |
| **Agent** | 每台机器上运行：配对一次、执行白名单命令、心跳。 |
| **Plugin** | 你的 agent 调用的那些工具。 |
| **Admission**（1.1.14+） | 新机器申请加入；在线成员批准，**10 秒自动同意**；入队 24 小时内的机器可被立即移除。 |

### 工具

`w2m_status` · `w2m_devices` · `w2m_run` · `w2m_wait` · `w2m_history` · `w2m_stats` · `w2m_report` ·
`w2m_memory` · `w2m_approvals` · `w2m_cancel` · `w2m_council` · `w2m_chat` · `w2m_update` `w2m_tasks`

### 被派发命令会收到的环境变量（1.1.15+）

取值来自 offer，**不来自 argv**，因此单台机器无法改变整个编队的分片：`W2M_INDEX` / `W2M_INDEX_TOTAL` /
`W2M_STAGE_INDEX` / `W2M_TASK_ID` / `W2M_MODE` / `W2M_MACHINE_ID` / `W2M_MACHINE_NAME`。

因此 `command_argv=["node","-e","process.exit(Number(process.env.W2M_INDEX)+1)"]` 在四台机器上应分别退出
1/2/3/4。**单机行为已测；四台机器的联跑尚未验证**（见下方"未验证"）。

### 编队模型

身份是**账号**，不是主机清单。机器从账号材料派生 Ed25519 身份；账号的第一台机器配对时，relay 登记对应公钥；
此后每台机器用一次性签名挑战自证同一个账号。

只有当旧配对路径因**明确原因**失败时 —— 配对码无效、relay 不可达、超时 —— 机器才降级去申请入队。其它失败需要
人工介入，**不会**切换机制。**拒绝即终态**，机器不会再次申请。

所有时间窗与法定人数由 relay 权威判定，因为客户端时钟互不一致（实测：同一编队内相差数十秒）：

- 无决策 **10 秒**后自动同意，但**仅当至少一名成员在线** —— 空编队无法同意，该拒绝有明确错误码
  （`NO_ONLINE_MEMBER`）；
- 入队后 **24 小时内**，任一在线成员可立即移除该机器；
- 超过 24 小时，单台机器只能**发起表决**，且法定人数集合在**发起时冻结**，投票者中途离线无法改变门槛；
- 法定人数：旧成员 ≥3 人需 **≥50%（向上取整）**；2 人编队的移除只要 **1 票**；
- 离线超过 **72 小时**的机器会离开**列表** —— 记录**永不删除**，它重新上报后会自动回来。

### 安全姿态

- 命令白名单按 **argv 前缀**匹配，并拒绝 argv 重解析标志（`--import`、追加 `-e`），错误码
  `COMMAND_REPARSE_ARGUMENT`。这是边界，不是沙箱。
- 派发任务需要 operator token；device token 不能派发。
- 审批入队要求至少一名成员在线。
- 账户签名密钥从 **fleet key** 派生，**绝不**用 account code —— account code 会写进日志，用可读值派生密钥等于
  交出账号身份。
- 每个发行版都有校验和。

### 已验证与未验证

**一句真话胜过一块掩盖问题的绿牌。**

**已验证：** 102 个文件中的 2458 项测试（2444 通过、14 跳过）、15 项门禁检查、Windows / macOS / Linux 三平台
CI 全绿、npm 与 GitHub 发布及校验和一致、在真实的 Linux/Mac/Windows 三机编队上跑过端到端。

**未验证 / 已知缺口：**

| 缺口 | 状态 |
|---|---|
| 审批**弹窗**控件 | relay 强制规则、`w2m_approvals` · `w2m_cancel` 可列出并裁决，但 10 秒倒计时是列表里的 relay 数据，不是独立弹窗 |
| 四台机器的 `W2M_INDEX` 联跑 | 单机行为已测；编队级 1/2/3/4 尚未执行 |
| 编队聊天 / 广播通道 | 消息存储与配额已实现并测试；加密、分片、端点与面板**尚未构建** |
| 部分 macOS 主机的 P2P | 观察到 `P2P_PUNCH_FAILED: Unknown cipher`；任务会降级走 relay 路径 |

### 故障排查

| 症状 | 原因 | 处理 |
|---|---|---|
| 装好了，但 `w2m_devices` 返回 401 | agent 从未启动，因此没有 device token | 确认 `autoStartAgent` 不是 `false`；**重启 DSH**（热重载无效） |
| 编队里看不到这台机器 | 插件没写进 `dsh.profile.bundles` | 加进去 —— 不在 bundle 里的包永远不会加载 |
| `COMMAND_NOT_ALLOWED` | 命令不在白名单 | 扩充白名单；argv 按前缀匹配 |
| 裁决总是 `partial` | 来自已下线机器的陈旧租约 | 1.1.2 已修：派发只对在线且未沉默的机器建租约 |
| `P2P_PUNCH_FAILED` | NAT，或宿主密码学能力缺口 | 会自动降级到 relay 路径，结果不受影响 |

### 发布通道（中文）

三个通道，其中只有一个是你 \
pm install\ 默认拿到的。

| 通道 | 来源 | 适合谁 |
|---|---|---|
| **stable** | npm \latest\，开发者明确声明为稳定版 | 所有人；默认安装就是它 |
| **beta** | GitHub **prerelease**（tarball + \SHA256SUMS\），**绝不进 npm** | 被授予 \ eta-access\、且接受它可能失败的开发者 |
| **最新构建** | 两者中版本较新的那个，不论通道 | 想要最新代码、并理解上述含义的开发者 |

**默认的 bump 是 beta**。只有开发者明确说明"这次是稳定版"，npm 才会收到该版本：beta 以 prerelease 形式发布（因此
GitHub 与 npm 都不会把它解析成 \latest\），只有在 \ eta-access\ 环境审批通过后才能下载，安装前需阅读
[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) 并自担风险。

beta 工作流里**没有 \
pm publish\ 这一行**，这是刻意的 —— 只要发布动作不可能发生，这个通道就不可能泄漏到默认安装。
### 链接

- [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) —— 每个版本，包括它**故意没有**交付的内容
- [PLATFORMS](docs/PLATFORMS.md) —— Claude Code、Codex 与 MCP 的接线细节
- [Releases](https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/releases) —— 每个版本的证据与校验和
- [Issues](https://github.com/TwinsEarth/dsh-windows2macos/issues)

# @deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Side tasks plugin, browser half: a temporary per-session task panel beside the main conversation. The conversation header gains a 「侧边任务」 action with a live count badge; clicking it opens a right-hand overlay panel owned by the current session, which **collapses to a compact top-right chip** as its resting state and expands while a task is being worked on.

Each side task is a **forked child session** (`session.fork` with title incrementation) — it runs its own agent with the owner's full context, independent of the main thread. Two properties make it a temporary task rather than a fork visible in the sidebar:

- **Hidden by default**: the child is archived (`workspace.archiveSession`) right after creation, so it never appears in the workspace sidebar or the ungrouped bucket — the panel is its only surface. The forked seed context is the task's working memory, not its display: the mini conversation shows only the task's OWN messages (everything after the task's LAST `session/end-seed` marker — an owner that was itself resumed or forked nests earlier markers inside the seed, so the first one would leak the owner's recent messages), so a new task is just a composer ready to talk.
- **Self-expiring**: a task with no activity (creation, send, or a settled turn) for one hour (`SIDE_TASK_TTL_MS`) is deleted automatically by the apply-side sweep while the page is open; persisted activity timestamps let a refresh resume the same expiry. Running tasks are never swept. Each task row shows its own live countdown (`还剩 N 分钟自动删除`, ticking every second from the persisted last-activity timestamp) so the expiry is never a surprise.

The lifecycle is the plugin's core selling point: **deleting a task leaves no residue**. The delete button (two-click confirm) calls `session.delete(childId)`, which disposes the host agent, removes the child from every workspace account, and erases its stored log — the task row, the panel selection, and the persisted collection entry all go with it. Closing the panel only hides the UI: tasks and their idle agents stay alive until their expiry sweep and reappear on reopen.

## Slot and data architecture

Two registrations share one apply-owned controller (a register-declared store mounts under exactly one scope, so cross-scope sharing goes through the controller):

- **`conversation.session.header.actions`** (session scope, id `side-task`, order 30): the trigger button + count badge. Reads the store through the injected `useSideTasks` hook; the owner passes nothing.
- **`shell.overlay`** (root scope, id `side-task-panel`): the right-hand panel OR the collapsed chip. Reads the store (`useSideTasks`), the selected task's conversation (`useTaskConversation` — a derived source that follows the store's `selected` binding), the session list (`useSessions`), and the injected verbs (create/delete/send/stop/select/collapse/expand/close).

The controller owns the `createSnapshotStore` instance, the conversation source, per-session localStorage persistence (ids + per-task activity timestamps), the expiry sweep, and the RPC verbs; components receive everything through the inject face and never touch `ctx`.

## Model Experience

Indirectly, through the `session.fork`, `session.prompt`, `session.cancel`, and `session.delete` verbs the panel invokes: creating a task forks a child session from the current session's prefix with an incremented title, sending a prompt queues a user turn in the task's own session, stopping cancels its running turn, and deleting removes the child's log and workspace accounts. The panel itself adds no prompt content of its own; everything the model sees comes from the user's own sends inside a task.

#### KV Cache effect

None from the plugin itself. Sending inside a task extends that child session's history tail like any other prompt, so admitted context can change its provider-side cache reuse; deleting a task removes its log entirely.

## Known Limitations and Deferred Work

- **Mini-conversation is text-only** — tool calls, context injections, reasoning blocks, and other surface nodes are intentionally omitted from the compact panel; the full transcript lives in the main conversation by opening the task session normally.
- **Expiry sweep runs while the page is open** — a task left idle with the browser closed stays until the next page load (the persisted activity timestamps resume the countdown then); there is no host-side janitor. — the event window only backfills the current session, so the panel fetches the selected task's durable history (`session.history`) on selection and refreshes when a running turn settles or after a send. A reply in progress shows a 「运行中」 indicator and appears in full once the turn ends.
- **Panel is single-owner** — it follows the current session (`useSessions.current`); switching sessions re-points the panel to the new owner's collection. There is no multi-pane side-task view.
- **Queued sends while running are disabled** — the composer locks during a running turn instead of offering the main composer's queue semantics; a task must settle before the next prompt.

## Installation

The repository ships prebuilt bundles (`lib/`), so a normal user installs
in two steps — no build toolchain needed:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/uluckystar/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-client-ui-side-tasks   # or your active profile
# restart the profile for the bundle metadata to take effect
```

**Standalone activation (MyDSH rc.6)**: the package includes a `dsh.bundle`
patch that mounts its inert host entry. That registration is required for DSH to
discover and load the browser module; a plain dependency installation alone is
not proof of activation. Restart the profile, then verify that the browser loaded
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks/client.js` and the session header shows the
side-task action. Some DSH builds already include a side-task UI: remove the
other registration before enabling a duplicate.

**Dependency note**: this plugin relies on the `session.delete` and
`session.history` capabilities, which must be available in the DSH build you actually use. Check these
capabilities before installation; a repository date or version label alone
is not an install/boot test. Without them, history rendering and complete
child-session deletion are unavailable.

### Building from source (developers only)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/uluckystar/dsh-client-ui-side-tasks
cd dsh-client-ui-side-tasks
pnpm install
pnpm bundle
```

Note: the official `@deepseek-ai/*` release candidates are published to npm
incrementally — if `pnpm install` reports a missing package (e.g.
`@deepseek-ai/dsh-compact`), resolve it from the official harness workspace
checkout or wait for the rc to be published.

## 社区维护与兼容性

本仓库是 MyDSH 非官方社区维护版本，与 DeepSeek 官方无隶属关系，保留上游 MIT 授权。它提供临时 fork 任务，不应被描述为长期讨论记忆系统。长期讨论记录、用户确认后保存的助手记忆等方案应作为独立能力评估。

不同 DSH 版本的客户端注入和槽位接口可能变化。安装前请在独立 profile 验证任务创建、主子会话归属、停止、删除与重载；仓库元数据或声明校验通过不能代替这些实测。

### Fixed-version validation and capability boundary

On DSH source commit `99f6f02fecdb7dff40c3fbc9470f5907c29f74ca` (CLI rc.7),
a clean isolated profile confirms installation, host-layer registration and
browser-module loading. That runtime does **not** expose the legacy client
`ctx.sessions.history` / `ctx.sessions.delete` methods this plugin's temporary
lifecycle requires. rc.6 therefore disables creation/deletion and explains the
missing capability instead of creating children that cannot be cleaned up or
throwing a browser TypeError. This is **not** a passing full lifecycle test on
that DSH version. Do not rely on one-hour expiry there.

Controller/UI tests use explicit service fixtures; they are not a claim that
every DSH build implements these methods. Supported versions still need their
own create, reload, close, deletion and idle-expiry acceptance.

That explicit capability gap blocks compatibility certification. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.
